These results demonstrate that ERM-mediated coupling of actin to the cell membrane provides an important mechanical link between the actin cortex and microtubule-driven centrosome positioning, influencing both centrosome centering and spindle geometry.

title: VQIL: Visible Quantum Interference Learning for Perturbation Response Ranking on Graphs
abstract: Learning how local perturbations affect a network is important for identifying which components drive or absorb a system's response. We formulate this as seed-conditioned response ranking: given a perturbation at one seed node, ranking all other nodes by response strength. This is challenging when the model is given only the interaction topology, while the mechanism governing how perturbations propagate must be learned from data. We present VQIL (Visible Quantum Interference Learning), a trainable Szegedy quantum walk for seed-conditioned ranking. Edge weights, link phases, and per-node phase rotations are optimized end-to-end by backpropagation while the walk operator remains unitary throughout training. Node scores are obtained from a geometrically discounted coherent sum of quantum-walk amplitudes, enabling quantum interference before the final squared-norm readout. Because each learned parameter is attached to a named edge or node, the trained model provides directly inspectable hypotheses about the roles of individual graph components in the propagation mechanism. On AC power-flow perturbations over six transmission grids, with electrical parameters withheld from the model, VQIL improves Spearman rank correlation from 0.147 for the untrained walk to 0.831 and outperforms an identically trained random-walk model. On gene perturbation over five protein-protein interaction networks with Perturb-seq supervision, VQIL improves rank correlation from 0.171 to 0.620, outperforming the strongest learned classical and neural baselines. These results show that trainable quantum-walk interference provides a scalable and interpretable inductive bias for learning seed-conditioned response rankings on graphs.

title: Electron-Density-Informed Molecular Property Prediction Using Surrogate Functionals
abstract: Machine learning methods are increasingly used to predict chemical properties directly from the molecular structure to bypass the often prohibitive cost of quantum mechanical calculations. Recent work has shown that including the ground-state electron density as input to the machine learning model can improve accuracy in this setting. This work employs the recent surrogate functional framework originally developed for orbital-free density functional theory and extends it to predicting molecular properties. We show that passing the ground-state density as input to the model, while simultaneously enforcing it to be the minimum of the surrogate functional, surpasses state-of-the-art performance for six out of seven extensive properties of the QM9 dataset. Additionally, the approach shows improved generalization to larger molecules taken from the QM40 dataset. On all extensive properties of both datasets, our approach outperforms models that are informed by the ground-state density but do not enforce the surrogate functional constraints.

title: Ferroelectric Domain-Wall Motion, Stability, and Frequency Responses under Different Screening-Charge Conservation Laws
abstract: We analyze ferroelectric domain wall motion, shape, and internal structure arising from coupling between polarization and screening charge. Universal cases are organized by electrical boundary conditions, charge conservation and dynamics, and polarization free energy. We consider exposed surfaces, interfaces beneath a dielectric layer and top electrode, and interfaces with a blocking mixed ionic-electronic conductor. Screening occurs through local exchange, exchange with lateral transport, or strictly conserved redistribution. Analytical derivations and finite-depth calculations establish screening drag, velocity branches, and conditions for spatial instability. For an isolated wall joining differently compensated domains, strict surface conservation and zero far-field current exclude steady translation of the screening profile, while allowing transient displacement, finite-sample arrest, and charge-balanced structural changes. Conservation also constrains long-distance transport around a moving junction in an adjoining conductor. Large-field simulations in the top-electrode geometry reveal nonlinear corrugation, transfer toward longer wavelengths, and coupled polarization rotation. First-order polarization energetics allow two interphase fronts enclosing a paraelectric core; multiaxial polarization permits wall rotation and competing intermediate ferroelectric domains. A driven structural-screening reduction supports stable periodic behavior. Reduced-variable diagrams summarize motion and structural regimes, while BaTiO3 and BiFeO3 examples connect them to material thermodynamics. Small-signal analysis distinguishes displacement, polarization, and electrostatic response functions. These results provide a framework for wall dynamics and structural transitions under different driving and screening conditions.

title: Model-agnostic Knowledge Augmented Machine Learning for Weakly Annotated Bioimaging Data
abstract: Machine learning models are increasingly used for automated feature extraction from weakly annotated bioimaging data, such as microscopy and cytomorphology images. Due to the sole dependency of automated feature extraction, existing methods yield inconsistent classification performance across weakly annotated datasets. Here, we propose a model-agnostic knowledge augmentation method that enables ML models to exploit domain knowledge beyond what automated feature extraction can capture. The proposed approach improves classification performance across seven ML architectures. When integrated with masked autoencoder-based self-supervised learning, our method achieves the strongest overall performance, improving precision by 2.9% over the next-best method on three in-house microscopy datasets and by an average of 6.8% across three public cytomorphology benchmarks. We perform nucleus-level classification based on mislocalization of TAR DNA-binding protein 43 (TDP-43) from the nucleus to the cytoplasm, a phenotype linked to Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS), using three independent microscopy datasets of motor neurons derived from human induced pluripotent stem cells. Accurate quantification of this phenotype at scale remains challenging and may contribute to inconsistencies across studies. Application of the best-performing model to these microscopy datasets reveals biological interpretations related to ALS, including dose-dependent effects of the proteasomal stressor, MG132, and the oxidative stressor, sodium arsenite (SA), on TDP-43 mislocalization, variable pathology in motor neurons from sporadic and familial ALS donors, and a lack of protection of the pharmacological compounds, edaravone and niclosamide, against SA-induced TDP-43 mislocalization. Together, our pipeline enables in-vitro cellular image analysis to advance understanding of ALS-associated pathology and potential treatments.

title: Engineering the Interfacial Microenvironment to Boost Ethane Dehydrogenation on Ga2O3-Pt Catalysts via Metal Doping Modulation
abstract: Inverse Ga2O3-Pt catalysts have exhibited better catalytic performance in propane dehydrogenation due to their tunable interfacial electronic properties. This study explores the potential of inverse Ga2O3-Pt catalysts and their single-atom-doped variant (Ga2O3-M/Pt) systems for ethane dehydrogenation using DFT calculations and kinetic Monte Carlo simulations. The results show that Ga2O3-Pt exhibits low ethylene formation activity (0.83 × 102 s–1) and selectivity (84.28%) due to its interfacial sites that weakly and uniformly adsorb hydrogen, impeding the differential regulation of key CH2CH3*…

title: Blockiness as Determinant of Liquid Phase Formation by Polypeptide-Like Polymers in Stickers-Spacers Paradigm
abstract: Liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) driven by intrinsically disordered protein regions underlies the formation of membraneless organelles. The role of these structures in cell biology is an active area of research, yet their physical understanding remains less developed than that of protein assemblies with well-defined, rigid tertiary structures. The amino acid composition of disordered regions, particularly the abundance of charged residues, is known to modulate phase behavior. These factors govern accessible conformations, the assembly of compact sticker clusters, and the porosity of the resulting polymer networks. In contrast, the spatial distribution of side-chain volumes remains a comparatively understudied sequence determinant. Here, we employ a model that captures the patterning of side-chain volumes and interaction strengths without specifying chemical identity to show how sequence blockiness modulates the phase-nucleation propensity, connectivity, and compactness of polypeptide-like polymer assemblies. Using a library of polymers with identical composition but permuted residue arrangements, we show that clustering of bulky residues generates cooperative sticker domains and identify the threshold blockiness required to stabilize polymer networks. Coarse-grained simulations and mean-field theory reveal that this effect arises from an interplay among steric repulsion, solvent entropy, and higher-valency interactions, whereby blocky patterns promote the formation of multi-node percolated networks. Segregation of stickers and spacers is therefore one of the sequence parameters governing LLPS which may be useful for interpreting the evolution of disordered protein sequences, high-throughput proteome screening, and engineering of stimuli-responsive biomaterials. These rules may be exploited to predetermine condensate stability, viscoelasticity, and molecular exchange rates without altering chemical functionality.

title: Anneal-MaxCal: kinetic ensembles from a Markov model learned along a solute-tempering ladder
abstract: A full characterisation of a molecular system requires its metastable states, their populations and their interconversion rates. Molecular Dynamics can in principle provide this characterisation but is limited by sampling and by force-field inaccuracies. Enhanced sampling addresses the first problem, but typically requires prior knowledge of reaction coordinates or metastable states and often sacrifices the kinetics, while maximum-caliber reweighting by Brotzakis, Vendruscolo and Bolhuis [Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. U.S.A., 118(2):e2012423118, 2021] has been implemented to that matter on reweighting continuous pathways by imposing rate constants as kinetic constraints in two-state protein folding. Here, we introduce Anneal-MaxCal, which tackles both problems by imposing rate constants or time-resolved data on a Markov model learned along an annealed solute-tempering ladder spanning softer to physical interactions. MBAR assigns physical free energies to all 160 cells of a slow TICA subspace, against 79 visited at the physical coupling. The square-root approximation (SqRA), a discretised diffusion on this free-energy landscape, converts these populations into a detailed-balance rate matrix. Its prefactors, which act as a position-dependent diffusivity across each cell face, are learned from transitions at the softer couplings and extrapolated log-linearly to the physical coupling. This yields rates and a committor across the TICA space, although the physical rung contains a single barrier crossing. For alanine dipeptide, 665 ns of simulation give a relaxation time of 5430 {+/-} 996 ps against 4413 {+/-} 446 ps from 15.4 s of unbiased dynamics, whereas a constant prefactor is 2.5 times too slow. Maximum caliber then minimally perturbs this prior, with the posterior populations following from a generalised Doob transform. A synthetic time-resolved density with a tenfold slower back-transition lowers {Delta}F from 5.191 to 2.885 kBT , raises the product-basin population from 0.0055 to 0.0529 and slows relaxation 9.47-fold, leaving the reactant basin unchanged. Forward and backward rates accelerated 3 and 20-fold raise {Delta}F by 1.892 kBT and shorten relaxation from 4818 to 289 ps.

title: Predicting the Risk of Proteinuria Based on Blood Plasma Fourier-Transform Infrared Spectroscopy and Machine Learning Algorithms From Pregnant Women and Newborns
abstract: Proteinuria, defined by an abnormally elevated concentration of proteins in the urine, serves as a critical biomarker for the early detection and diagnosis of preeclampsia. Elevated proteinuria levels adversely affect both maternal and foetal health, increasing the risk of preterm birth and low birth weight. This study focused on the identification of proteinuria in blood samples through Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy as a diagnostic tool for real-time diagnosis. Blood plasma collected during birth was evaluated in four study groups: pregnant controls (n = 12), pregnant women with proteinuria (n = 13), newborn controls (n = 12), newborns with proteinuria (n = 14). First, attenuated total reflectance-FTIR spectra of plasma samples were collected for subsequent spectral smoothing, vector normalisation and machine-learning classification with various supervised machine learning algorithms, including several types of Support Vector Machine, K-Nearest Neighbours and decision trees. We obtained (76.1 ± 3.1)% accuracy, (72.1 ± 4.8)% sensitivity and (80.4 ± 3.8)% specificity for pregnant classification, and (90.6 ± 1.5)% accuracy, (83.3 ± 2.4)% sensitivity and (98.9 ± 1.6)% specificity for newborn classification. The vibrational modes corresponding to the predominant biochemical components in blood plasma of pregnant women and newborns were listed. Sensitivity and specificity results demonstrated that FTIR can be a promising tool for early diagnosis and monitoring of individual proteinuria. Although the proposed spectroscopic approach demonstrated promising diagnostic performance, the findings should be interpreted in light of clinical conditions that could affect the biochemical profile. Further studies involving larger and more heterogeneous populations are required to validate the proposed methodology.
authors: Das Chagas E Silva de Carvalho LF

title: Improved screening of doped ZrO$_2$ catalysts for CO$_2$ hydrogenation from graph-based machine learning
abstract: Dopants can tune the activity of zirconia-based CO$_2$ hydrogenation catalysts through changes in adsorbate and transition-state (TS) energetics. Computing these quantities with density functional theory (DFT) becomes expensive when several dopants, reaction intermediates, and TSs must be screened. Here, we further develop the graph-based machine learning method Wasserstein Weisfeiler-Lehman Gaussian Process Regression (WWL-GPR): we introduce additional electronic-structure and local-environment features relevant for oxide surfaces and use the resulting model to predict adsorption and TS energies on ZrO$_2$(101) surfaces doped with Al$^{3+}$, Cd$^{2+}$, Ga$^{3+}$, In$^{3+}$, and Zn$^{2+}$. Adsorbate-surface structures are represented as attributed graphs that combine bonds connectivity and features. We benchmark WWL-GPR against thermodynamic scaling relations (TSR) for reaction intermediates and Bronsted-Evans-Polanyi relations (BEP) for TSs, and then propagate the predicted energies to microkinetic CH$_3$OH-yield estimates. WWL-GPR consistently improves the prediction of reaction intermediate energetics relative to linear scaling approaches and provides TS estimates that are competitive with BEP-based models. These improvements become especially relevant when the predicted energetics are propagated through the reaction network. Microkinetic calculations show that WWL-GPR-derived energies give CH$_3$OH yields closer to DFT-derived yields than the linear-relation workflow. Degree-of-rate-control analysis links the activity errors to dopant-dependent rate-controlling steps, including HCOO* formation, H$_2$COOH* dissociation, and H$_3$CO* formation. These results support WWL-GPR as a data-efficient surrogate for connecting atomistic energetics with catalyst-screening observables on doped oxide surfaces.

title: ReplaySSM: Cache SSM Inputs, Not State
abstract: State-space models (SSMs) maintain a fixed-size recurrent state, but reading and writing it at every decoding step can bottleneck hybrid models. This eager state management causes large state I/O with low arithmetic intensity, leaves speculative decoding no cheap rollback, and feeds state quantization error into subsequent recurrent updates. We introduce ReplaySSM, which unrolls the recurrence to represent the state as a checkpoint and a buffer of recent SSM inputs. This separates output computation from checkpoint updates. By updating the checkpoint periodically, ReplaySSM avoids state writes on most steps and roughly halves the dominant state memory traffic. Keeping recent inputs also makes speculative rollback a buffer-pointer operation and enables output-only verification without materializing intermediate states. The same separation allows a low-precision checkpoint to serve output computation on most steps while a higher-precision checkpoint serves recurrent updates, so rounding error in the low-precision copy never enters later updates. We implement ReplaySSM in vLLM for Mamba-2 and Gated DeltaNet. At serving batch size 256, it accelerates standard decoding by $1.20$--$1.47\times$ over a tuned vLLM baseline across four hybrid models, and delivers about $1.8\times$ the throughput of vLLM's speculative decoding on the two 120B-class models. Separate state precisions also reduce output KL divergence and downstream accuracy losses compared with a shared low-precision checkpoint.

title: Machine Unlearning for Federated Socially Fair k-Means Clustering
abstract: Federated clustering can support applications such as patient stratification across hospitals and customer segmentation across distributed financial datasets. Responsible AI calls for fair representation of demographic groups and support for data deletion, motivated in part by rights such as the GDPR's right to erasure. These goals interact: deleting records can change the balance between groups and alter the clustering of the remaining population. We study exact machine unlearning for federated socially fair $k$-means, whose objective is to minimize the largest group-average squared distance to the nearest center. Our approach keeps separate local summaries for each group, so summaries at unaffected institutions remain valid as global fairness weights change. For two groups, we prove an initialization approximation guarantee independent of client group proportions under ideal sampling, and we show that same-seed replay reproduces retraining exactly. Reuse pays off most when a whole client withdraws: across three datasets, replay is $35.8\times$ faster than retraining for the initialization-only model and remains $2.4\times$ and $1.7\times$ faster with one and two fair-refinement rounds, which improve worst-group cost. For individual record deletions, gains are modest (about $1.06\times$), and certifying cached assignments can cost more than it saves. These results map where exact unlearning can profitably reuse computation. Code and reproducibility materials are available at https://github.com/arareddy/mufsc.

title: Dislocation mediated twin boundary faceting in $β$-Sn
abstract: Grain boundaries (GBs), including twin boundaries (TBs), play a critical role in plastic deformation by interacting with dislocations. The deformation and strengthening mechanisms in $β$-Sn are of significant interest because Sn-based alloys are widely used as solder materials. Recent experiments have shown deformation-induced faceting in $β$-Sn arising from twin-dislocation interactions. Using molecular dynamics (MD) simulations informed by a recently developed machine-learned interatomic potential (MLIP), we demonstrate a $\langle c\rangle$ dislocation-absorption mediated faceting reaction along $(301)$ TBs in $β$-Sn in which facet length grows with the number of absorbed dislocations. We show that the predicted facet length is consistent with isotropic elasticity theory only when the disclination character of the asymmetric twin facet is taken into account. We discuss analogies to faceting reactions in other low symmetry metals and hypothesize that the ubiquity of $(301)$ twins in $β$-Sn stems from their ability to grow rapidly through a forest of dislocation obstacles.

title: Synthesis of Chiral α-Aminophosphonate Derivatives through Copper(I)-Catalyzed Enantioselective Alkylation
abstract: Efficient methodologies for the catalytic asymmetric synthesis of α-aminophosphonic acid derivatives remain limited, particularly those involving carbon-carbon (C-C) bond formation. Herein, we report a copper(I)-catalyzed enantioselective alkylation of N-protected aminomethylthiophosphonates with alkyl halides, which provides a versatile strategy for accessing diverse chiral α-aminophosphonate derivatives. A wide range of alkyl halides, including allyl bromides, propargyl bromide, benzyl bromides, and alkyl iodides, act as efficient alkylating agents.

title: SCKAnalyzer: A Web Tool for Single-Cycle Kinetics Analysis and Simulation
abstract: Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) and biolayer interferometry (BLI) are well-established label-free analytical technologies used to determine biomolecular interaction rates (ka, kd) and equilibrium constants (KD). While assays historically rely on multi-cycle kinetics (MCK), this approach requires intermediate surface regeneration, risking sensor degradation and increasing reagent consumption. Single-cycle kinetics (SCK) avoids regeneration by sequentially injecting increasing analyte concentrations.

title: Structural thermodynamics by cryo-EM resolves minute energy differences in heterogeneous protein complexes.
abstract: Hetero-oligomeric protein complexes play crucial roles across biology, providing combinatorial diversity and context-specific functionality in membrane receptors, molecular chaperones and beyond. Yet, existing methods are limited in their ability to resolve and quantify the assembly energetics of complex biomolecular populations. Here, we introduce a comprehensive method combining iterative 3D classification, error-rate quantification via simulated particles, and global thermodynamic modeling to extract interaction energies from cryo-EM data. Using hexameric cruciferin (the primary rapeseed storage protein) as a model, we reconstruct a 1.83 [A] structure and distinguish three highly similar 50 kDa isoforms. We resolve the complex compositional heterogeneity of the hexameric species at the single-particle level and fit a global binding model revealing pairwise interaction energies between isoforms differing by fractions of the thermal energy (kB T ). This method offers a powerful, broadly applicable tool to characterize the compositional heterogeneity and energetics of biomolecular complexes.

title: Potassium Molybdenum Chalcogenides: Electronic Structure Modulation through Cluster Dimensionality
abstract: Herein, we report a systematic structural and electronic investigation of potassium-inserted extended molybdenum chalcogenides synthesized via microwave-assisted solid-state routes, focusing on KMo6S8, K2Mo15S19, and K2Mo6S6. Using X-ray absorption spectroscopy, scanning electron microscopy, and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, we evaluate how systematic variations in Mo/S ratio modulate phase morphology and local electronic structure.

title: Nonadditive Conformational Effects of tRNA Core Modifications
abstract: Post-transcriptional modifications are known to regulate the structure and function of tRNA molecules. Compared to modifications in the anticodon region, the mechanistic effects of modifications in the core region of tRNA remain poorly understood. Using all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations on yeast tRNAPhe, we investigated the conformational effects of incorporating chemical modifications in the core region (termed hereafter “core modifications”) of tRNA. Specifically, we focused on three core modifications, namely, 7-methylguanosine (m7G), 5-methylcytosine (m5C), and 1-methyladenosine (m1A). We discovered that individual modifications increased the structural stability of tRNA, but their combinations produced multimodal free energy landscapes with multiple distinct basins. We identified m1A58 as a bifunctional regulator that locally disrupts structure while globally coordinating anticorrelated arm movement. The combination of m1A58 and m5C49 exhibited the lowest structural deviation from the crystal structure, while the triply modified variant incorporating all three modifications produced the most integrated residue community network, reflecting nonadditive allosteric coupling that cannot be predicted from any pairwise combination. Critically, core modifications established extensive allosteric pathways that prevent the consistent inward displacement of the anticodon stem loop otherwise observed in all simulations of chemically unmodified tRNA. Our results demonstrate that core modifications function as regulators of conformational ensembles rather than simple stabilizers.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Predicting Nanofabrication Variance: A Conditional Diffusion Model
abstract: Micro- and nanostructures fabricated by focused ion beam (FIB) milling invariably deviate from input designs due to systematic and stochastic effects such as ablation-rate fluctuations, and redeposition. As such, nominally identical iterations of a given process yield a distribution of non-identical fabrication outcomes, leading to variations in the physical (optical, mechanical) properties of fabricated structures. Existing models of the milling process typically predict a single deterministic fabrication result, neglecting this variability. Here we present a conditional diffusion model that learns the statistical distribution of process outcomes conditioned on input design, enabling it to predict a realistic distribution of possible output sample structures. These predictions accurately reproduce edge morphology, linewidth variations, and defect probabilities observed in fabricated samples, enabling statistical analysis of milling performance and the identification of dominant structural and process parameter-dependent deformation modes. The work establishes a probabilistic modelling framework for fabrication variability analysis and fabrication-aware design optimization.

title: Quantitative Eshelby stability: local and finite-shape theory through AI-assisted mechanics
abstract: How can human researchers use artificial intelligence (AI) to make progress on difficult mechanics problems while retaining control of physical significance, mathematical rigor, and validation? We explore this opportunity through a quantitative stability problem rooted in the Eshelby conjecture. For a uniform dilatational eigenstrain in a homogeneous isotropic solid, we establish a nonlinear two-sided relation between whole-interior strain heterogeneity and a geometry-only distance from the ellipsoid family, with half-order Sobolev scaling that captures morphological length scale. We then develop a complementary finite-shape theory: ellipsoidal subtraction yields an exact residual-field budget from which systematically convergent upper and lower bounds are obtained for a prescribed geometry. Applied to protruded, indented, and necked inclusions, the bounds agree with independent displacement-based finite-element calculations. The study also documents a human-led, AI-assisted research process in which researchers select consequential problems, shape targets, audit arguments, require independent checks, and interpret mechanics, while AI broadens analytical exploration and supports computation. This experience also led us to develop Open Problems in Mechanics, a versioned community-facing map that makes selected mechanics questions, their known/open boundaries, and criteria for progress explicit.

title: VN-GraphGG: von Neumann--Mullins--based graph grain growth simulation
abstract: Efficient simulations of grain growth are essential for investigating the process-structure-property relationships in polycrystalline materials. We introduce a two-dimensional von Neumann-Mullins-based graph grain growth simulation (VN-GraphGG), which couples the grain-scale kinetics with microstructure reconstruction. The polycrystalline microstructure is represented as a graph with grain and junction nodes. The grain-area evolution on the grain graph is governed by the von Neumann--Mullins (VN) law, while a graph neural network is trained to reconstruct the microstructure from the graph. This separation allows kinetic coefficients to be varied without retraining the neural reconstruction model. Topological changes during grain growth such as disappearance of grains and changes in neighbor relations are handled straightforwardly through reconstruction and postprocessing. Simulations demonstrate accurate predictions of VN kinetics and coarsening statistics, and significant speedup over the phase-field simulations. The proposed method provides a foundation for efficient grain growth simulation based on grain-scale kinetics, opening the way to incorporate a broader range of physical mechanisms. An application example is presented for abnormal grain growth, in which kinetic heterogeneity significantly influences the grain microstructure evolution.

title: Magnetic-field-induced detwinning of orientational domains in altermagnet $α$-MnTe: A single-crystal neutron diffraction study
abstract: Altermagnets combine compensated magnetic order with momentum-dependent spin splitting, which makes them promising for future spintronic and magnonic applications, but their macroscopic responses can be strongly reduced by domain averaging. In hexagonal $α$-MnTe, three symmetry-related in-plane Néel-vector orientations and their time-reversal counterparts form six magnetic domain states, complicating both magnetic structure determination and measurements of the chiral magnon response. Using single-crystal neutron diffraction, we show that an in-plane field applied along the $[-1,1,0]$ direction produces a common magnetic domain orientation that saturates near $μ_0H=2$ T. A constrained refinement of 61 nuclear and magnetic reflections collected at 2 K and 2 T yields $\mathbf{M}\parallel[1,1,0]$, an ordered moment of $4.62(8)~μ_\mathrm{B}$ per Mn, and an orientational domain population at $r_A:r_B:r_C=0.97:0.03(5):0$ that is compatible with a nearly complete alignment of orientational domains. Furthermore, an abnormal behaviour in the temperature dependence of the selected reflections is observed in 60-88 K, its microscopic origin is discussed within the context of possible intrinsic piezomagnetic or magnetoelastic effects. Because unpolarized diffraction neither distinguishes domain repopulation from continuous Néel-vector rotation nor resolves time-reversal antiphase domains, the field-prepared state is a near-single-orientation state rather than a truly single-domain state. This non-contact domain control provides a practical complement to strain and field-cooling approaches for preparing well-defined magnetic states in bulk $α$-MnTe.

title: Unveiling the Influence of Graphitic Nanocarbon Structures, Defects, and Surface Functional Groups on Supercapacitive Performance in LiTFSI Electrolyte
abstract: When investigating the performance of supercapacitors (SCs), it was found that they offer high-power density and long life but are limited in capacity and energy density. Water-in-salt electrolytes, i.e., 21___m lithium bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl) imide (LiTFSI), offer a solution by expanding the electrochemical window compared to a diluted aqueous environment. While significant research has been dedicated to improving these electrolytes, the impact of carbon properties on energy storage remains relatively underexplored. This study investigated the influence of carbon structures, defects, and surface functional groups on supercapacitive performance in LiTFSI electrolytes. For this purpose, a series of carbon materials, including carbon nano-onions and porous conductive carbon black (ENSACO), were synthesized and systematically modified by oxidative and reductive thermal treatments. Our results indicated that higher specific surface area and active surface area improve the ion adsorption and capacitance, while specific oxygen functionalities, such as carboxylic and anhydride groups, were found to significantly enhance capacitance. Furthermore, crystallinity and graphitic characteristics play a role in capacitance, with smaller graphene domains and greater disorder promoting ion storage. The study demonstrates a direct correlation between carbon microstructure and electrochemical behavior, providing insights into the rational design of carbon electrodes in high-performance SCs.

title: Controlling the Atomic Reconstruction in Twisted MoSe$_2$/WSe$_2$ with a Monolayer hBN Spacer
abstract: Twisted van der Waals heterobilayers are a promising material platform for studying collective exciton many-body phenomena, but near-aligned structures often exhibit a local, anisotropic atomic reconstruction that compromises lateral homogeneity. The present study describes how atomic-scale rearrangement in adjacent regions of hBN-encapsulated, near-aligned MoSe$_2$/WSe$_2$ heterobilayers is controlled by the presence of a mono- or bilayer hBN spacer between the two monolayers. High-angle annular dark-field STEM directly resolves the atomic alignment in both layers and shows that the spacer suppresses the reconstruction and strongly increases the structural uniformity of the heterobilayers. 4D-STEM quantitatively maps local rotation, dilation, and heterostrain, revealing that the separated regions remain consistent with rigid moiré superlattice simulations, whereas without the spacer the structural parameters have two to three times broader distributions. By suppressing reconstruction, ultrathin hBN spacers therefore provide an effective route to enhance lattice homogeneity in MoSe$_2$/WSe$_2$ heterobilayers targeting collective excitonic and optoelectronic phenomena.

title: The effects of non-stoichiometric lattice structure and secondary phase α-Fe2O3 on modifying the magnetic, electrical, and magneto-electric properties of Eu doped BaFe12O19 hexaferrite
abstract: The Ba-atoms in BaFe12O19 were substituted by Eu-atoms to prepare the material of composition Ba1-xEuyFe12O19. The Eu atoms occupied at the sites of Fe atoms. The atomic ratio of Eu/Ba were varied from 0 to 0.33 to control the secondary phase (hematite) and M-type hexaferrite. Raman spectra provided complimentary support for a systematic increase of the hematite phase on increasing the Eu/Ba ratio. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy informed the presence of oxygen deficiency and surface defects, and charge state of Ba and Fe/Eu ions close to +2 and +3, respectively. The material showed direct optical transitions with band gap in the range of 2.25-3.09 eV. The increase of Eu/Ba ratio systematically increased the saturation magnetization from 84.44 emu g-1 to 57.68 emu g-1 at 3 K and 67.09 emu g-1 to 43.42 emu g-1 at 300 K, along with remarkable enhancement of the coercivity (914- 3656 Oe at 3 K and 1996-4862 Oe at 300 K). Electrical conductivity increased from 10-11-10-10 Sm-1 at 30 K to 10-5 -10-4 Sm-1 at 300 K. The electrical conductivity analysis reveals the Efros-Shklovsky-type variable-range hopping mechanism at the low-temperature region, whereas the Mott variable range hopping mechanism is applicable near to room temperature. The analysis of current-voltage characteristics provided electrode to sample interfacial barrier height of 0.27-0.74 eV. The material exhibited novel magneto-electronic properties (bi-stable electronic switching and its transformation in the temperature scale, magnetoresistance and magnetoelectric coupling) which are highly useful for spintronic devices. This work demonstrates that controlled Eu/Ba atomic ratio in the stoichiometric and non-stoichiometric lattice structure could be an effective strategy to widely tune the magnetic, optical and magneto-electronic properties in M-type Ba hexaferrite material.

title: Taking the heat off tantalum
abstract: Krypton-assisted growth of low-loss α-phase tantalum on silicon stays within back-end-of-line semiconductor thermal budgets while delivering state-of-the-art qubit coherence.

title: Reproducible and Interpretable H&E-based Histopathological Subtypes of Non-metastatic Lymph Nodes Refine Risk Stratification in Colorectal Cancer
abstract: Lymph node status is fundamental for staging, prognostic assessment, and treatment decision-making in colorectal cancer (CRC); however, current pathological evaluation largely focuses on metastatic involvement and overlooks the biological heterogeneity of non-metastatic lymph nodes (LNs). Here, we developed a reproducible histopathological classification system for non-metastatic LNs and established an interpretable machine-learning model for patient-level risk stratification in CRC.
venue: Modern pathology : an official journal of the United States and Canadian Academy of Pathology, Inc

title: A permeable G310 constriction limits K+ flux in the activated KCNQ2 pore and is disrupted by the encephalopathy variant G310S
abstract: KCNQ2 (Kv7.2) subunits contribute to the channels that carry the neuronal M-current, and variants in KCNQ2 cause epilepsies that range from self-limited neonatal seizures to developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (DEE). Structures of KCNQ2 bound to PIP2 and cannabidiol show a widened activation gate, yet it has remained unclear which point of the activated pore limits K+ flux and how DEE variants at that point act. We simulated the KCNQ2 pore domain (PDB 8J01) in a POPC bilayer under an applied field of about 565 mV, restraining only the terminal residues of S5 and S6 so that G310 and S314 were free. The activated pore conducted K+ at 4.3 pS (95% CI 2.5-6.9; 17 net filter crossings in 1120 ns over four replicas), while the closed-state pore (PDB 7CR3) conducted none in 560 ns. Conduction proceeded by knock-on through a filter that was doubly occupied in 84-92% of frames. Along S6 the narrowest position of the activated pore was not the canonical gate residue S314 but the glycine of the Pro-Ala-Gly motif, G310: activation widens S314 by 0.37 nm but G310 by only 0.07 nm, and restraining G310 to its closed-state width in one replica abolished gate crossings. The DEE variant G310S reduced conduction about six-fold (G310S/wild-type ratio 0.16, 95% CI 0.02-0.66; p = 0.003). Its serine hydroxyls project into the constriction and halve the water column in the G310 plane (8.7 to 4.7 waters), an effect reproduced in CHARMM36m (9.9 to 4.3). The first coordination shell of a K+ ion at the constriction was, however, conserved (6.3 vs 6.5 oxygens), because the serine hydroxyls replace the waters they displace. The hydroxyls did not retain the ion: contacts lasted tens of picoseconds, and ions were instead turned back at the serine ring, fewer reaching the gate plane (45 vs 79 excursions per microsecond) and fewer of those crossing it (5% vs 23%). In mixed tetramers carrying one or two variant subunits the effect on the water column was additive, each subunit removing about a quarter of it (f = 0.22 and 0.58 of the full effect). These results identify G310 as the flux-limiting constriction of the activated KCNQ2 pore in our simulations and point to a permeation defect as one component of G310S loss of function.

title: LiH/FePcG-Catalyzed Ammonia Synthesis via Interfacial Hydride-Mediated Dinitrogen Activation
abstract: Ammonia synthesis under mild conditions remains challenging because of the inertness of the N≡N bond and the limited ability of conventional catalysts to couple efficient dinitrogen activation with rapid hydrogenation. Here, we report a LiH/FePcG catalyst in which strong interfacial coupling between LiH and Fe–N–C sites enable efficient ammonia synthesis. title: PEDOT with Sulfonated PVA and Choline Chloride Enables Printable and Stretchable Electronics
abstract: Poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene):polystyrene sulfonate (PEDOT:PSS) has become an important conductive polymer dispersion for constructing flexible electronic devices; however, its electrical and mechanical performance still falls short of practical application requirements. Herein, a highly conductive and stretchable PEDOT film is prepared through a molecular-level material design strategy, using sulfonated poly(vinyl alcohol) (SPVA) as the PEDOT dopant to replace PSS and subsequently blending PEDOT:SPVA with choline chloride (ChCl).

title: Giant geometric nonlinear transport in inhomogeneously strained Bi$_2$Se$_3$ single crystalline slabs
abstract: Electrical transport in non-centrosymmetric materials exhibits a nonlinear conductivity tensor component that generates second-harmonic voltages in response to applied electric fields. Harnessing this effect is essential for developing zero-threshold electromagnetic energy harvesters and broadband frequency upconverters, both of which require maximizing the nonlinear responsivity. Here, we demonstrate that inhomogeneously strained macroscopic slabs of the topological insulator Bi$_2$Se$_3$ achieve a record-high nonlinear responsivity of $10^4\,μ$m/V: a six orders of magnitude boost compared to its thin-film counterparts. We attribute this giant enhancement to a classical geometric nonlinear transport effect, which is driven by complex strain gradients within the bulk material. Notably, a similar geometric mechanism known as geometric nonlinear Hall was previously observed only in microscale-patterned structures. Our findings establish macroscopic strain engineering as a powerful route to enhance nonlinear transport, with immediate relevance to a broad class of layered systems, including transition metal dichalcogenides and moiré heterostructures.

title: Latin squares as a model of perfect mixing of high-entropy alloys
abstract: The structure of high-entropy alloys, which include 5 or more components in equimolar proportions, is proposed to be described in the mathematical language of Latin squares. This model is fundamentally discrete and allows for a quantitative description of ideal mixing, in which any given alloy element is guaranteed not to have an identical element as its nearest neighbor. For the two-dimensional case, the model possesses four axes of translational symmetry, which makes it possible to tile the plane with a single Latin square and, based on the properties of this square, describe the properties of macroscopic material samples. The model makes it possible to make quantitative estimates of the suitability of a particular atomic structure (configuration) for implementation in a perfectly mixed high-entropy alloy with maximum mixing entropy. A condition has been obtained for acceptable fluctuations in the concentration of components at which the thermodynamic stability of the alloy is maintained. The possibility of identifying superstructures in high-entropy alloys based on group theory, as applied to the description and construction of Latin squares, is discussed. Based on the proposed model, the probability of forming a multicomponent alloy with ideal mixing is estimated. For a five-component alloy, this probability is no more than 2.6*10^{-10}.

title: Aubry-André transition in photonic time quasicrystals
abstract: In one dimension, Anderson localization by a disordered potential sets in at any strength, whereas localization by a quasiperiodic potential in the Aubry-André model occurs through a transition at a critical strength. Disordered photonic time crystals exhibit a temporal counterpart of this Anderson localization, in which light, instead of decaying in space, stops propagating and grows in time. Whether a counterpart of the Aubry-André transition exists in photonic time quasicrystals remains an open question. Here we show that it does, and that the transition occurs at mobility edges in momentum rather than in energy. These edges arise even under impulsive modulation, where the field obeys the self-dual almost-Mathieu equation exactly, and for general analytic modulations Avila's global theory reveals the condition under which they form. The Aubry-André transition thus extends from spatial lattices to the time domain, where it sorts light by wave number into components that propagate and components that stop and grow.

title: COMPLAX: A Python Tool Package for Automated Microsolvation of Organic Molecules
abstract: Since the solvent choice drives organic reactivity, accurate computational modeling of explicit solute–solvent interactions remains crucial but preparation-intensive. We present COMPLAX, an open-source Python tool that automates the generation and optimization of targeted microsolvated clusters around highly localized active sites. Unlike unconstrained global optimizers, COMPLAX employs a rigid-core approach to preserve delicate solute geometries. To ensure unbiased spatial sampling, it couples a deterministic Fibonacci spherical lattice with three-dimensional rotational randomizations. Generated structures are refined via a two-stage xTB geometry optimization, utilizing a constrained pre-relaxation step to prevent unphysical solvent detachment. By automating conformer ranking and energy evaluations via a simple command-line interface, COMPLAX provides a reproducible, out-of-the-box solution for explicit microsolvation workflows.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Allosteric Inhibition of the Oncogenic JAK2 V617F Pseudokinase Domain via Polar Heterocycles: Thermodynamic Deconvolution and Cross-Domain Selectivity Profiles
abstract: Background: Constitutive hyperactivation driven by the somatic V617F mutation in the Janus kinase 2 (JAK2) pseudokinase (JH2) domain disrupts the vital autoinhibitory interface governing the adjacent catalytic (JH1) domain. Because standard therapeutics target the structurally conserved orthosteric ATP pocket of JH1, they frequently induce severe kinome-wide off-target toxicities. This study establishes a rigorous biophysical framework to define the thermodynamic and structural parameters required to achieve mutation-specific allosteric targeting within the V617F pseudokinase cleft.

title: Reversible Sn4+/Sn0 anode for high-energy-density flow batteries
abstract: Tin-based aqueous flow batteries offer high-capacity anodes due to the potential four-electron redox reactions, but irreversible Sn4+/Sn2+ electrochemistry has hindered battery development. Now it has been shown that iodide-mediated intermediate complexes enable reversible Sn4+/Sn2+ conversion and four-electron Sn4+/Sn0 chemistry, yielding a high anolyte energy density and stable long-term operation.

title: Retrieval-to-abstraction LLM-assisted literature synthesis: Case demonstrations in digital health technology-enabled randomized controlled trial outcome reporting
abstract: Systematic reviews of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) support evidence-based clinical advancement. Clinical trial reporting guidelines, including CONSORT, establish common data elements that support systematic synthesis of published trial outcomes. However, the rapid rise of digital health technologies presents new challenges for reporting guidelines, and substantial real-world reporting heterogeneity has been observed. Therefore, machine-assisted evaluation of reporting adherence offers a pathway for more agile information management to accommodate the diverse and disruptive nature of digital health technology-enabled RCTs. Here, we propose an accelerated retrieval-to-abstraction literature synthesis framework to conduct article screening, text and table data preprocessing, and full-text review using an unmodified pretrained large language model. We apply this methodology in two digital health technology-enabled RCT case studies evaluating adherence to technology and digital health equity guideline reporting items. Large language model performance was on par with inter-annotator agreement F1 scores (≥0.9) in both screening and information-extraction tasks. These findings support the scalability and rigor of accelerated evidence synthesis and demonstrate the importance of common reporting elements across digital health technology-enabled RCTs.

title: Light-Induced Self-Healing Behavior in Photosalient Coordination Polymer
abstract: Achieving self-healing in the photosalient (PS) crystals without compromising structural integrity is a challenge. So far, self-healing and photomechanical behaviors have predominantly been reported as independent phenomena. Systems that concurrently exhibit both properties under a single stimulus remain uncommon. Here, we report the integration of the photomechanical property with a self-healing behavior by embedding dynamic covalent disulfide (S–S) linkages into a photoreactive coordination polymer (CP).

title: Scalable Thermoset Informatics Integrated with Autonomous Experimentation for On-Demand Discovery
abstract: As photopolymer additive manufacturing matures, there is an increasing need for on-demand, application-specific materials. A major bottleneck is the limited exploration of the vast design space for new thermoset polymer formulations, which must satisfy both material property requirements and processing constraints. This challenge arises from the combinatorial complexity of formulations and the high cost of experimental evaluation. In this work, we present an end-to-end pipeline that integrates a partial self-driving laboratory (p-SDL) with informatics-driven optimization to discover and validate thermoset acrylate formulations. The pipeline begins with a thermoset acrylate database that consolidates multiple data sources, including in-house experiments, molecular dynamics simulations, and literature data. These data sets are used to train single-task and multitask predictive models, which interface directly with the p-SDL to guide experiments and measure mechanical and processing-related properties. Each component is validated independently and then deployed together to optimize a target elastomeric material with over 90% reduction in human effort. The complete optimization required only ∼40 h of active experimental time, demonstrating rapid identification of formulations that satisfy multiple target properties without exhaustive screening. This work establishes a scalable framework for embedding multifidelity machine learning within laboratory workflows, enabling autonomous, data-driven thermoset formulation discovery.

title: Diffusion-Limited Solid-State Synthesis Selectivity in the Presence of Oxidation/Reduction Processes
abstract: Solid-state synthesis outcomes arise from an interplay between thermodynamics and kinetics, with their relative importance governed by external control parameters such as temperature profiles and precursor selection. A recently introduced framework, combining first-principles thermodynamics with machine-learning-enabled simulations of correlated ion transport, successfully captured this interplay in the Ba–Ti–O system by linking phase selectivity to ion mobility within “liquid-like”, amorphous interphases. Notably, in systems where valence states can change during synthesis, ion dynamics are strongly coupled to oxidation state. Here, we extend the framework to such mixed-valence systems and demonstrate its predictive power for the synthesis of ternary metal ferrites in the Ba–Fe–O and Y–Fe–O systems, benchmarked against in situ XRD experiments. Similar to the Ba–Ti–O system, we hypothesize that the rate-limiting transport of ionic species governing polymorph growth occurs through a “liquid-like,” noncrystalline interphase. To capture this behavior, we employ a charge-informed machine-learning potential (CHGNet) that enables modeling of correlated, redox-dependent transport. We find that the framework accurately predicts the sequence of phase formation and the time evolution of phase distributions in powder synthesis reactions, in agreement with experimental reports. These results show that diffusion-limited phase selectivity can be treated on a unified footing across mixed-valence oxides, further clearing a pathway toward rational, in silico synthesis design that simultaneously accounts for thermodynamic and kinetic factors.

title: Atomic Site-Specific Eigenstrain for Efficient Electrocatalysis
abstract: Strain engineering is a powerful approach to tailoring the performance of metal electrocatalysts. Despite substantial advancements in controlling the average surface strain and establishing its correlation with catalytic activity, the impact of strain at individual active sites remains elusive. Here, we demonstrate the influence of site-specific strain on catalytic reactivity in Pt nanoclusters by quantitatively modulating and mapping the atomic-scale strain.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Crystal Phase-Dependent Electronic Metal-Support Interactions Enable Chemoselective Hydrogenation of α, β-Unsaturated Aldehydes
abstract: Electronic metal-support interactions (EMSI) provide an effective means of tuning the electronic structure of supported metal catalysts and thereby modulating their catalytic properties. However, how the crystal phase of supports governs EMSI and in turn influences the selective hydrogenation remains largely unexplored. Here, we report a crystal-phase engineering strategy to precisely regulate EMSI in ultrafine Ir nanoclusters (NCs) supported on polymorphic Nb2O5.

title: Direct Colloidal Synthesis of High-Entropy Carbide Nanoparticles with Altered CO2 Hydrogenation Selectivity
abstract: The controlled synthesis of refractory carbide nanoparticles remains a longstanding challenge in colloidal nanoscience because strong metal–carbon bonding and high formation energies complicate nucleation, growth, and compositional control. Here, we report the direct colloidal synthesis of single-phase high-entropy (HE) carbide nanoparticles, (CrMnMoW)C1–x, (TiCrMnMoW)C1–x, and (CrMnFeMoW)C1–x, via the simultaneous thermolysis of transition metal carbonyl precursors in oleylamine.

title: Evaluation of large language models for ICI-related liver injury with an emerging microbiome focus
abstract: BackgroundImmune checkpoint inhibitor-related liver injury (ICI-LI) has heterogeneous phenotypes, a complex differential diagnosis, and evolving management. Gut microbiome research provides biological plausibility for immune regulation during ICI therapy, but evidence specific to ICI-LI remains limited and is not yet clinically actionable. We evaluated whether publicly accessible large language model (LLM) chatbots can organize this mixed evidence base and communicate its uncertainty.MethodsWe developed a disease-specific benchmark of 25 questions covering immunological mechanisms, microbiome and immune regulation, diagnosis, biomarkers, and management of ICI-LI. The benchmark addressed ICI-LI broadly and included a focused microbiome component. Four publicly available LLM platforms were evaluated using DISCERN, EQIP, the Global Quality Score, the JAMA Benchmark Criteria, and six readability indices. These instruments assessed information quality, structure, transparency, and patient-facing readability rather than factual accuracy or clinical decision-making.ResultsPerformance differed across DISCERN, EQIP, and JAMA scores, whereas the Global Quality Score showed limited discrimination. Question-level variation was most apparent for items requiring evidence appraisal or translation. All platforms produced structured responses, but none met the prespecified patient-facing readability benchmark. Readability was interpreted separately from clinician-facing information synthesis.ConclusionsDisease-specific multidimensional evaluation is needed before LLM-generated information can be considered reliable for microbiome-informed clinical communication or decision support. Evaluation should emphasize evidence calibration and distinguish biological plausibility, association, and clinically actionable evidence.
venue: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology

Chemistry in Pictures: One man’s trash
Digital twins in toxicology: Toward predictive, personalized and real-time risk assessment
abstract: Toxicology has accumulated many predictive tools - physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) models, quantitative systems pharmacology (QSP) frameworks organ-on-chip systems, quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) models, adverse outcome pathway (AOP) networks and machine-learning approaches. Yet predictive practice remains fragmented. Each tool captures a slice of biology; few capture the whole; none captures the patient.

title: An Immune-Vascular CD80/HTR2B Axis Integrates S-Palmitoylation and Vascular Inflammation in the Pathogenesis of Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm: Evidence from Mendelian Randomisation, Multi-Omics, Single-Cell Perturbation and qPCR Validation
abstract: Background: Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is characterised by irreversible dilatation of the abdominal aorta and a risk of rupture. Clinical assessment still relies mainly on diameter and growth rate and does not capture the immune, vascular and matrix heterogeneity of the aortic wall. Protein S-palmitoylation is catalysed by ZDHHC palmitoyltransferases and reversed by depalmitoylating enzymes. It regulates membrane localisation and trafficking of immune receptors, chemokine receptors, ion channels and vascular signalling proteins.

title: 3D CNN-CVAE and LSTM-guided de novo design of rotigotine derivatives targeting dopamine D1 and D3 receptors in restless legs syndrome
abstract: Restless legs syndrome (RLS) is a chronic neurological disorder associated with altered dopaminergic signaling, while long-term dopamine agonist therapy may be limited by augmentation and reduced clinical benefit. This study applied a three-dimensional convolutional neural network conditional variational autoencoder integrated with long short-term memory molecular generation to design rotigotine-derived candidates targeting dopamine D1 and D3 receptors. Fourteen unique derivatives were generated and screened through pocket prediction, molecular docking, interaction profiling, pharmacophore analysis, density functional theory, ADMET prediction, 500 ns molecular dynamics simulations performed in explicit water without a lipid bilayer, and MM/GBSA calculations. Docking protocol validation using DockRMSD yielded RMSD values of 1.009 Å for Mevidalen in the D1 receptor and 1.359 Å for PD-128907 in the D3 receptor, supporting acceptable reproduction of both experimental binding poses. In docking-based ranking, AI Derivative 1 was placed above rotigotine for D1 (-5.744 vs -5.629 kcal/mol) and D3 (-7.934 vs -7.288 kcal/mol) and formed additional hydrogen-bond and hydrophobic contacts; the D1 difference of approximately 0.1 kcal/mol lies within the intrinsic uncertainty of docking scoring functions and is not interpreted as evidence of improved affinity. Docking scores are used throughout as ranking and prioritization metrics rather than quantitative binding free energies. It also exhibited a smaller HOMO-LUMO gap, a higher predicted LD50, and a shift from toxicity class 3 to class 4. Molecular dynamics analyses, including RMSD, RMSF, radius of gyration, solvent-accessible surface area, hydrogen bonding, DCCM, PCA, and free-energy landscapes, are reported as descriptive observations from single non-membrane trajectories and are not used to claim physiological relevance or superior binding stability. MM/GBSA estimates were favorable under the applied computational conditions. AI Derivative 1 therefore represents a computationally prioritized lead requiring experimental validation.

title: Advances in monitoring the injured brain
abstract: Multimodal neuromonitoring has emerged as a cornerstone of modern neurocritical care for traumatic brain injury (TBI). Traditional monitoring approaches based on intracranial pressure (ICP) and clinical examination alone have proven insufficient to capture the complex, heterogeneous pathophysiology that drives secondary brain injury. Over the past decade, significant advances in monitoring technology, including brain tissue oxygenation, cerebral microdialysis, continuous electroencephalography, near‑infrared spectroscopy, cerebrovascular autoregulation assessment and non‑invasive techniques…

title: Regio- and Enantioselective Functionalization of Gaseous Alkanes via Nickel-Catalyzed Alkene Dicarbofunctionalization
abstract: The regio- and enantioselective functionalization of gaseous alkanes remains an unsolved challenge in organic synthesis. Here, we report a general strategy for the asymmetric three-component dicarbofunctionalization of alkenes using readily available gaseous alkanes, including ethane, propane, and isobutane. This transformation, enabled by the merger of hydrogen atom transfer photocatalysis with a chiral nickel catalyst, efficiently delivers chiral α-aryl carbonyl compounds in good yield with excellent regio- and enantioselectivity (up to >20:1 rr and 99:1 er). Experimental and computational studies reveal insights into the mechanism controlling selectivity. Operating under exceptionally mild, energy-efficient conditions, the method unlocks a versatile platform for upgrading feedstock gaseous alkanes into sought-after chiral building blocks.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Necessary conditions for benchmarking next-generation AI in materials discovery
abstract: Current AI predicts materials by speeding up energy minimisation and training on large databases. However, scaling data generation prevents manual analysis by domain experts. If novelty is evaluated by chemical compositions or traditional representations in Crystallographic Information Files, or standard structure matchers based on manually chosen thresholds, one can easily generate millions of ``new'' compositions or files without discovering truly novel materials. This paper uses a hierarchy of crystal invariants to continuously trace and quantify structural novelty based on the new mathematical definition of a crystal structure and asymptotic guarantees for invariant descriptors. The invariant-based analysis through cascade computations on a modest computer exposes the unexpected scale of duplication in the world's largest materials databases, shown here in the high-profile case of GNoME datasets. To prevent current ``embarrassment of over-prediction'', we propose necessary conditions for next-generation AI that should be automatically enforced before claiming any new materials.

title: Inference-Time Steering Across Scaffolds and Epitopes for Sample-Efficient De Novo Nanobody Design
abstract: Generative molecular design typically relies on over-generation and post-hoc filtering. Inference-time steering methods like Feynman-Kac (FK) steering improve efficiency by biasing trajectories toward high-reward candidates, yet they optimize within a single fixed configuration. In de novo nanobody design, upfront commitment to conditioning choices like scaffold identity or target epitope creates a bottleneck. Since yield varies across these conditions, steering unpromising setups wastes compute. We recast generative condition selection as an inference-time resource-allocation problem. We propose two dynamic budget allocators: a joint Global Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) formulation that steers and allocates compute across configurations concurrently, and a decoupled approach adapting Batched Successive Elimination (BaSE). Empirically, these dynamic allocators increase the yield of designable candidates per GPU-hour nearly 5$\times$ without sacrificing diversity across distinct therapeutic targets and generative configurations.

title: Doubly Metastable Synthesis for Accelerated Quantum Materials Discovery
abstract: New physics emerges from new materials, which in turn rely on the development of new synthesis techniques. Identifying the enlargement of metastable synthesis window as enabling for realizing novel materials, we develop diffusion-activated epitaxy, a technique which combines two metastable synthesis methods of diffusion and epitaxy. We observe that within a narrow window of investigated synthesis space we can experimentally identify the stabilization of four distinct phases, three of which show X-ray diffraction and scanning transmission electron microscopy characterization data that are incompatible with the crystal structures registered in experimental and computational inorganic structure databases. These results suggest an enlarged metastable synthesis window is enabled by this synthesis approach, identifying doubly metastable synthesis as a promising method for exploration of quantum materials.

title: Phononic Frequency Combs in Twisted Bilayer Transition Metal Dichalcogenide Heterostructures from First Principles
abstract: Phononic frequency combs are equidistant spectral ladders generated when a driven vibrational mode transfers energy to an autoparametrically excited subharmonic mode through anharmonic intermode coupling. In previous studies, the coupling strength governing this energy transfer has typically been treated as a free parameter, extracted from a fabricated device, or adopted from an earlier calculation for a specific mode pair. As a result, whether a given crystal can support a phononic frequency comb, and the drive strength required to generate it, has not been predictable a priori. Here we obtain the complete parameter set from density functional theory. Twisted bilayers of \MoSSe{} and \MoSMoSe{} at the commensurate angle $21.787^{\circ}$ adopt space group $P3$ in a 42-atom \rootseven{} moiré supercell. The second-order force constants provide the mode frequencies; the third-order constants provide the linewidths through the Boltzmann transport equation and hence the quality factors; and the same third-order tensor projected onto the phonon eigenvectors of a chosen mode pair provides the anharmonic couplings $\kt$ and $\kss$. Both bilayers constitute a mode pair within $0.8\%$ of the $2\!:\!1$ resonance with $ω_1/ω_2 = 1.9923$ in \MoSSe{} and $1.9943$ in \MoSMoSe{}. By integrating the resulting two-mode equations, both modes generate combs through a discontinuous transition: at $701\,\fth$ in \MoSSe{} the envelope variance rises from $2.1\times10^{3}$ to $1.37\times10^{4}$ and the tooth count of mode 1 from 7 to 16 within a single $5\,\fth$ increment, identifying the onset as subcritical. The spectral entropy peaks \emph{before} this jump, at $341\,\fth$. The two compounds carry comparable coupling, differing by a factor of $1.2$. However, the comb excitation threshold is set by the quality-factors of signal modes: $Q_2 = 672$ for \MoSSe{} and $Q_2 = 3844$ for \MoSMoSe{}.

title: Single-Cell and Bulk RNA-Seq Profiling Identifies Cell Adhesion-Related Gene Signatures in Cerebral Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury
abstract: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) involves complex secondary damage mechanisms, including oxidative stress, inflammation, and blood-brain barrier disruption, in which cell adhesion-related genes (CARGs) play a central role. Therefore, systematically elucidating the expression and regulation of CARGs is crucial for identifying new therapeutic targets to mitigate inflammatory infiltration and preserve barrier integrity. Both single-cell and bulk transcriptomic data were obtained from the Gene Expression Omnibus database. The single-cell data were processed using Seurat, and CARG activity was comprehensively assessed using five scoring algorithms, including UCell and AUCell. A combined machine learning framework incorporating Boruta algorithm, LASSO regression, and random forest was employed to screen for reliable diagnostic biomarkers. Furthermore, immune infiltration profiles were evaluated using CIBERSORT, regulatory networks were constructed, and molecular subtypes were identified through consensus clustering. Single-cell analysis revealed high CARG activity in endothelial cells, smooth muscle cells, and astrocytes. Machine learning identified four robust diagnostic biomarkers (Itgb1, Fn1, Pdlim5, Kdr) with excellent predictive accuracy (AUC, 1) across multiple datasets. These biomarkers strongly correlated with immune cell infiltration, particularly macrophage polarization and mast cell activation, and successfully stratified CIRI samples into two distinct molecular subtypes. By integrating single-cell and transcriptomic data, this study systematically reveals the critical role of CARGs in CIRI. It identifies four core diagnostic genes that are closely associated with immune microenvironment remodeling and neuronal damage, thereby providing new molecular markers and a theoretical foundation for clinical diagnosis and treatment.

title: Evolution and breakdown of chiral anomaly in Weyl semiconductor tellurium
abstract: Chiral anomaly in topological materials manifests as negative longitudinal magnetoresistance, yet the tunability and evolution of this effect remain elusive. Here we show that doped tellurium serves as a versatile platform to realize a giant negative longitudinal magnetoresistance that is highly tunable via the Fermi level and magnetic field. By moving the Fermi level towards the Weyl point, we observe a pronounced enhancement of negative magnetoresistance, which arises from chiral anomaly and robustly persists up to ambient temperature. Beyond the quantum limit, the system exhibits positive linear magnetoconductance, serving as a compelling transport signature of the chiral anomaly in the lowest Landau level. Notably, in the extreme quantum limit at cryogenic temperatures, the magnetoresistance undergoes a dramatic reversal from negative to positive. This reversal points to a potential field-induced phase transition into a collective electronic state driven by enhanced electron-electron interactions. Our findings provide valuable insights into the unconventional chiral transport and emergent correlated quantum states under extreme magnetic fields.

title: Designing Protein Structures from Natural Language
abstract: A central challenge in de novo protein design is generating proteins with desired structural and functional properties. Existing design models typically require a dedicated input representation for each property, limiting the design objectives they support. We develop Prompteina, the first all-atom structure generation model that supports new and broader design objectives specified in natural language, analogous to text-to-image generation. To train Prompteina, we construct Prompteina-Data, a paired text--protein structure dataset of 1.8M structures and 50M+ captions describing global and residue-specific structural and functional properties. We adapt Proteina-Complexa, a pretrained structure generation model, through text-conditioned pretraining and finetuning that aligns residues with their corresponding text. Prompteina outperforms baselines on 15 of 18 structural properties and generates proteins that more closely match descriptions of their intended functions. In binder design, it leads baselines on at least 13 of 20 targets and improves interface confidence by 14% over the strongest baseline. With iterative in silico feedback, Prompteina's gain over non-iterative generation is 57% larger than the next-best baseline on the hardest targets. Finally, we experimentally validate Prompteina designs against GM2A, a target with no reported de novo binders. We identify nine binders, with the strongest at an apparent $K_{\mathrm{D}}$ of 107 nM. These results establish natural language as an effective and powerful conditioning interface for protein structure generation.

title: Accuracy of Vibrational Properties of Machine-Learning Force Fields for Molecular Crystal Transformations
abstract: Machine-learning force fields (MLFFs) enable the calculation of transformation pathways in molecular crystals at a fraction of the computational cost of density functional theory (DFT). However, a good agreement in energies and structures does not necessarily imply an accurate description of vibrational properties, which are essential for characterizing transition states and determining free energies at finite temperatures. Herein, we assess the accuracy of system-specific SO3krates MLFFs trained on PBE+MBD reference data for describing vibrational properties of molecular crystal transformations. As examples, we consider a polymorph transition of 1,4-diiodobenzene and a single-crystal-to-single-crystal Diels-Alder reaction. The transition state structures obtained from solid-state nudged-elastic-band (NEB) calculations with the MLFFs exhibit a single imaginary $Γ$-point frequency associated with the respective transformation. Compared with PBE+MBD, the mean absolute errors of $Γ$-point vibrational frequencies and relative harmonic free energies at 300 K are about 3 cm$^{-1}$ and 1 kJ/mol, respectively. Furthermore, we compare for the Diels-Alder reaction a collective transformation pathway with a sequential one, in which individual diene-dienophile pairs react successively, and demonstrate that PBE0+MBD single-point corrections can significantly affect the predicted reaction energetics. These results demonstrate that system-specific MLFFs can reproduce not only the energies and forces but also the local curvature of the potential-energy surface with high accuracy, enabling reliable calculations of harmonic vibrational free energies, providing a basis for extending the studies of molecular crystal transformations to larger supercells.

title: Hide and Seek: HIDE Concepts to SEEK explanations for black box models
abstract: Interpreting machine learning model predictions is a central challenge, particularly for black-box vision models. Concept-based attribution methods interpret models using human-understandable concepts. Existing concept-based methods can only interpret classification and regression models. They require access to model weights or large concept-annotated datasets, and most methods cannot provide image-level attribution. We propose Hide and Seek (HnS), a new method for concept-level attribution that does not require access to model weights or labeled concept datasets. HnS can interpret a wide range of vision models. Given a concept and image set, HnS retrieves concept-aligned images using a vision-language model, localizes the concept within each image, masks the localized region, and measures attribution from the change in the black-box model's output between the original and masked images. This enables faithful attribution by directly measuring the model's behavior and supporting local attributions. We validated HnS on CelebA and COCO-Stuff. Compared to existing methods, HnS showed better agreement with ground-truth attributions. We demonstrated the applicability of HnS on diverse tasks, including image captioning and satellite image segmentation, where no existing concept attribution method can be used. We provided our anonymous code in the supplementary material.

title: AI Models Can Provably Hide Arbitrary Capabilities
abstract: Capability evaluations aim to surface dangerous model behaviors before deployment, but their reliability depends on the assumption that hidden capabilities can be elicited. We show this assumption does not hold under adversarial conditions by constructing backdoor attacks that embed encrypted neural networks within host model weights, decrypting and executing them only upon receiving a secret trigger. Using digital lockers, these hidden circuits remain provably hard to elicit and interpret under cryptographic assumptions, even given full access to model weights, extending prior work from hiding fixed strings to arbitrary computations. We implement our proof of concept constructions in PyTorch and evaluate elicitation through fine-tuning, weight noising, gradient-based trigger search, and latent adversarial training, using a small chemical reaction prediction task as a proxy for CBRN-relevant capabilities. Our results demonstrate resistance to these methods and, together with our cryptographic guarantees, reveal a limit of elicitation-based capability audits. We release our models to support the improvement of defenses.

title: Spin Migration in the Argon Dimer
abstract: We introduce the concept of \emph{spin migration}, i.e. time-dependent spin density, and the absolute smallest example of molecular spintronics. We illustrate the concept by \emph{ab initio} calculations of the coupled vibronic motion of the electrons and the nuclei in the argon dimer cation, in which the vibrational level spacing is similar to the spin--orbit splitting of the atomic argon cations. We find that the spin density varies on multiple time scales, given by the natural time scales of the electronic and nuclear wavepackets.

title: Capturing Ag6 Inner-Core Contraction in Inorganic-Template-Stabilized Ag78 Nanoclusters
abstract: Resolving how subangstrom changes in a metal core affect electronic structure and photophysical properties in high-nuclearity silver nanoclusters (NCs) remains challenging, as inner-core variations are often coupled with changes in outer metal shells, surface coordination, or crystal packing. Here, we report a structurally homologous series of Ag78 NCs (Ag78-1–Ag78-4) sharing a common Ag6@Ag24@Ag48 metal architecture stabilized by an S2–/SO42– inorganic template framework.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Synergistic RhFe Single-Atom Alloy and Nanoalloy Sites for Highly Efficient and Robust Heterogeneous Hydroformylation
abstract: Transforming homogeneous olefin hydroformylation into a robust heterogeneous process is hindered by Rh leaching and CO-induced suppression of H2 activation. Here, we report a dual-site RhFeSAA+NA/hydroxyapatite (HAP) catalyst featuring spatially differentiated RhFe single-atom alloy (SAA) and nanoalloy (NA) sites that overcomes the fundamental conflict between CO tolerance and reactivity.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: A deep learning-generated hASIC1a miniprotein inhibitor confers neuroprotection in stroke
abstract: Ion channels remain notoriously recalcitrant drug targets despite their extensive pathophysiological significance. Acid-sensing ion channels (ASICs) are proton-gated cation channels that cause neuronal death when excessively activated, such as during ischaemic stroke. This acidosis-driven injury pathway remains unchallenged by existing therapeutics. Here we generate two de novo designed hASIC1a-specific miniproteins by developing a platform that integrates computational miniprotein design, high-throughput automated patch clamp screening, biophysical and structural characterisation, and in vivo validation. We identify a subtype-selective hASIC1a inhibitor, Denasin1, which achieves near-complete inhibition with nanomolar potency. Denasin1 is disordered in solution but adopts the computationally predicted helix-turn-helix fold when bound to the extracellular acidic pocket of hASIC1a. Crucially, Denasin1 reduces infarct volume by > 50% in a murine model of ischaemic stroke.
