We thereby establish our de novo design platform as a route to develop potent and selective ion channel modulators.

title: Electronic structure and multiscale modelling of the hydroxyapatite-TiO2 bio-interface: from self-interaction error to predictive coating design
abstract: Hydroxyapatite-titanium dioxide (HA-TiO2) heterojunction coatings are commonly applied to enhance the osseointegration of load-bearing orthopedic implants, but their clinical performance is limited due to coating delamination and fibrous tissue encapsulation at the implant-bone interface. Density functional theory (DFT) offers excellent pre-synthesis predictions on HA-TiO2-based designs, but self-interaction error (SIE) remains a major hurdle due to the well-known underestimation of the band gaps of TiO2 and oxygen vacancy formation kinetics. This leads to inaccurate predictions of localized oxidative stress, electron transport, and early-stage corrosion at the interface. A comprehensive review of the accuracy-cost trade-off of DFT+U, hybrid functionals (HSE06), and machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) for modelling the HA-TiO2 interface is given here. The electronic-structure corrections related to mesoscale phenomena accessible by molecular dynamics (MD) are also described. A systematic description of the stiff, ice-like hydration layer formed at the TiO2 surfaces is provided to shed light on the transport of Ca2+ and PO4 3- during biomineralization. Further, the dynamics of the hydroxyl dipoles, doping and nanostructuring that affect the nature and strength of the resulting interfacial adhesion energy are elaborated in detail. This multiscale approach that connects the accuracy of the electronic structure with the mesoscale hydration and ion-transport kinetics offers a physics-based, computationally informed path to the rational design of HA-TiO2 biomaterial coatings.

title: Senescence-induced Spatio-temporal Re-organization of the Nuclear Lamina Dynamic Landscape at Single-molecule Level in Live Human RPE Cells
abstract: A defining hallmark of cellular senescence is the extensive remodeling of the nuclear lamina (NL) in both structure, composition, and its interactions with lamina-associated genomic domains. However, how such senescence-induced changes could quantitatively impact the spatio-temporal dynamics of NL interactions at the single-molecule level remain poorly understood. Herein, using human retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) cells as model system, we establish a robust, chemically inducible cellular senescence model capable of recapitulating key signatures of the senescence-associated phenotype. Senescent RPE cells exhibit distinct alteration patterns in the expression of various NL components, including lamin B receptor (LBR) and emerin, two key mediators of NL-chromatin interactions. Importantly, live-cell diffusion measurements via imaging FCS reveal globally enhanced mobility for both LBR and emerin, indicative of weakened NL anchoring in senescent cells. Single-molecule tracking and super-resolved STAR mapping further unveil distinct, multi-modal re-organization of their NL-binding dynamics in both space and time (especially in the form of LBR binding "hotspots" where multiple stable binding events cluster to effect more extended and prolonged interaction), in line with their respective expression-level alterations and differential lamin interactions. Moreover, correlative mapping uncovers a strong spatial coupling between reduced LBR mobility and highly condensed constitutive heterochromatin domains at the NL, which become dispersed during senescence. Collectively, these findings demonstrate the re-organization of NL dynamic landscape at single-molecule level as a critical and previously under-explored facet of senescence-induced NL remodeling, and point to a synergistic interplay between physical de-anchoring, dynamic attenuation of stable NL-binding and spatial restructuring of chromatin architecture in modulating NL-heterochromatin contacts to potentially effect global changes in senescence-associated gene expression.

title: Ultra-lightweight Flexible Perovskite–Perovskite–Organic Triple-Junction Tandem Solar Cells
abstract: Triple-junction photovoltaics offer a promising route to surpass the efficiency limitations of single-junction solar cells, yet existing high-performance architectures are predominantly rigid and relatively heavy, limiting their use in weight-sensitive applications. Here, we report, to the best of our knowledge, the first ultra-lightweight and flexible monolithic perovskiteperovskite–organic triple-junction tandem solar cells.

title: MolSanitizer: An open-source pipeline to prepare small-molecule databases for large-scale virtual screening
abstract: Accurate preparation of small-molecule databases for virtual screening is crucial for the success of computer-aided drug discovery. Although numerous free software options are available, they often underperform compared to commercial alternatives. Here, we introduce MolSanitizer, an open-source molecular preparation pipeline built on RDKit and designed for large-scale virtual screening.

title: Mixed Ionic–Electronic Memory in a Conjugated Polymer Composite for Retrospective Optical Event Reconstruction
abstract: Coupling a light-responsive conjugated polymer to an ionic matrix and oxide interfaces offers a materials strategy for retaining complementary information about completed optical events. A PEDOT:PSS/Nafion/TiO 2 composite implements this approach through an irradiance-dependent conductance amplitude and a wavelength-dependent fading trajectory. At matched nominal polymer loading, TiO 2 incorporation reduces the light-OFF amplitude by 70–77% while extending the half-decay time by 1.56–2.01-fold.

title: Pd-Cu-Ag Trimetallic Synergistic Catalysis for Decarboxylative/Deaminative Coupling of Carboxylic acids with Tertiary Amines
abstract: Palladium-catalyzed coupling reactions, such as the well-established Suzuki and Hiyama couplings of benzylic ammonium salts, have been widely employed for the synthesis of diphenylmethanes. In contrast, the decarboxylative coupling strategy for constructing such scaffolds remains largely unexplored. This paper reports a Pd-Cu-Ag trimetallic synergistic catalytic system that enables efficient access to diphenylmethane derivatives through C(sp3)–N bond cleavage of amines and decarboxylation of carboxylic acids.

title: Quantitative Characterization of Pharmaceutical Powder Surface Interactions Using Inverse Gas Chromatography-Derived Surface Energy Profiles
abstract: Quantitative characterization of surface and interfacial properties is important for understanding the behavior of pharmaceutical powders, but conventional approaches to powder wettability and surface free energy can be influenced by measurement procedures and sample-specific factors. Inverse gas chromatography (IGC) provides a sensitive approach for characterizing powder surface energetics as a function of fractional surface coverage; however, the reproducibility and interpretation of IGC-derived surface energy profiles require careful evaluation.

title: Indium-Catalyzed Deaminative Coupling of Propargylamines with Terminal Alkynes: A Mild Approach to Conjugated 1,3-Dienones
abstract: A mild and efficient indium-catalyzed coupling of propargylamines with terminal alkynes has been developed, affording a diverse array of conjugated 1,3-dienones in good to excellent yields. The reaction proceeds via in situ hydrolysis of propargylamines to generate the corresponding enones, followed by an indium(III)-promoted syn-selective alkyne insertion. Using InCl3 as the catalyst and DBU as the base, the protocol features broad functional-group tolerance and operates under mild conditions.

title: The Pnictogen Oracle Provider: Multi-Fidelity Graph Landscapes To Benchmark Molecular Optimization
abstract: The informed discovery and inverse design of new molecules and materials is among the most active applications of data-driven procedures, such as statistical learning, to chemical problems. These approaches involve two key aspects: the dataset, and the exploration algorithms. Here, we cover both of these dimensions by introducing POP (Pnictogen Oracle Provider), a platform comprised by an extensive graph database and an optimization toolkit.

title: Density Functional Theory Bond Dissociation Energies of Model Compounds Relevant to LDL Oxidation: Bis-Allylic C–H, Phenolic O–H and Hydroperoxide O–H Bonds
abstract: Background: Oxidative modification of low-density lipoprotein (LDL) contributes to atherogenesis, with polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) as its main chemical target. Vitamin E is an effective chain-breaking antioxidant in vitro, yet large clinical trials showed no cardiovascular benefit. We calculated bond dissociation energies (BDEs) of model compounds to quantify the underlying thermodynamics.

title: The helium ground-state energy to 60 significant figures on a laptop
abstract: We report a variational upper bound on the nonrelativistic, infinite-nuclear-mass ground-state energy of helium whose first 60 significant figures are converged, E0 = −2.903 724 377 034 119 598 311 159 245 194 404 446 696 925 311 117 290 339 042 34 Eh, 16 more than the best previous record. The calculation runs on a laptop and the method, which we call FLAKE (Fock-log anisotropic Kronecker eigensolver), combines four ingredients.

title: Depth-resolved operando grazing-incidence diffraction reveals non-equilibrium Cu-Pt alloy restructuring under glycerol electrooxidation
abstract: Alloying Pt with Cu enhances activity towards hydrogen generation and valueadded products during the electrooxidation of glycerol, but the most active alloys typically require electrochemical activation, during which their structure and composition evolve in poorly understood ways. Here we use synchrotron-based operando, angle-dependent grazing incidence X-ray diffraction in a custom dual-chamber electrochemical flow cell to follow, in real time, the depth-resolved structural evolution of Cu-Pt thin-film catalysts under glycerol electrooxidation in alkaline media.

title: Selective Ligand Replacement Leads to Carbene Complexes as Catalysts in Proteins
abstract: Artificial metalloenzymes (ArMs) that incorporate organometallic fragments through direct metal–protein coordination open the door to unlock the full evolutionary potential of the protein scaffold to modulate catalysis. This work builds on our previously published work, in which Ru(II) piano stool complexes bearing bipyridyl ligands were used to deliver [Ru(Arene)]2+ fragments into a naïve protein scaffold, generating a transfer-hydrogenase artificial metalloenzyme.

title: Metalsurfer: Fast Generation of Realistic Substrate-Adsorbate Interfaces
abstract: Realistic adsorbate–substrate geometries are essential for meaningful electronic-structure calculations at interfaces, yet constructing them remains slow and generally ad hoc for bulky molecules, high coverages, and irregular surfaces. This challenge limits systematic exploration of adsorption configurations across many problems in catalysis, surface chemistry, and materials design. We introduce metalsurfer, a Python package that generates density functional theory (DFT)-ready interface models from simplified molecular input line-entry system (SMILES) strings and a substrate.

title: Formation Pathways of Cyanocoronene (C24H11CN) in the Interstellar Medium and its Detectability with JWST
abstract: Cyanocoronene, the currently known largest cyano-substituted polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH), has recently been discovered in the molecular cloud TMC-1. In this work, we investigate its possible formation pathways using density functional theory (DFT) together with multireference CASSCF and NEVPT2 quantum chemical calculations. Six distinct formation mechanisms are explored, including HAVA-type growth pathways as well as alternative bottomup routes.

title: Research Progress and Applications of the Fundamental Principles of Soft Ionization Mass Spectrometry
abstract: (1. Guangdong Huisheng Testing Technology Co., Ltd.) Abstract: Soft ionization mass spectrometry is widely applied in fields such as pharmaceuticals, cosmetics, environmental monitoring, and food safety; however, its fundamental principles remain subject to considerable debate, rendering it a "black-box" technology. This review summarizes the basic principles of electrospray ionization (ESI), matrix-assisted laser desorption (MALDI), and desorption electrospray ionization (DESI), and establishes "one theory, two equations, and three instruments" as the theoretical and practical foundation for…

title: Earth-abundant 3d metal-catalyzed enantioselective catalysis towards the functionalization of E/Zalkenes mixtures.
abstract: Enantioselective catalysis transforming alkenes to chiral molecules have been a breakthrough in the field of organic synthesis. Though a major challenge persists. The “privileged” chiral catalyst capacities depend on the geometry of the olefin substrate which can be either E or Z. Enantioselective catalysis allowing to convert both alkene stereoisomers to a single chiral molecule promises sustainable synthetic routes and novel mechanistic strategies towards chiral molecule synthesis.

title: Structure-Activity Relationship Studies of the Complement Regulator-Recruiting Peptide 5C6
abstract: Active recruitment of host complement regulators to biomedical surfaces emerges as a therapeutic strategy to prevent adverse immuno-inflammatory reactions to biomaterials and organ transplants. Coating with the macrocyclic peptide 5C6, which binds and recruits the central complement regulator factor H (FH), was shown to protect clinically relevant surfaces from complement attack. While we previously identified general determinants for the 5C6-FH interaction, more granular structure-activity relationship (SAR) studies have hitherto been missing.

title: Structural Convergence of MD simulations on RNA Motifs: A tRNA case study
abstract: A detailed understanding of the structural dynamics of diverse RNA architectures is critical for elucidating the chemical basis of cellular function and expanding the use of RNA in medicine and biotechnology. While classical molecular dynamics (MD) simulations can provide this much-needed atomic information, sampling requirements remain poorly characterized for RNA systems.

title: Alkyl-BODIPYs as a Self-Photoredox Catalyst for their Oxidative Hydroxymethylation
abstract: The adoption of photocatalytic approaches for utilising small organic molecules in self‑catalysed reactions offers opportunities in green organic synthesis. We report that alkylated boron‑dipyrromethenes (BODIPYs) act as self‑photoredox catalysts for their own oxidation under mild visible‑light conditions. Using an imidazolinium salt (NHC-H) as a quencher, alkylated BODIPYs are oxidised cleanly to the corresponding hydroxymethyl derivatives in a one‑pot process.

title: Total Synthesis of Site-Specifically Modified bHLHLz Transcription Factors Reveals Insights into the Regulatory Role of Posttranslational Modifications in the Myc–Max–Mad Network
abstract: The Myc–Max–Mad bHLHLz transcription factor (TF) network regulates the expression of ~15% of the human genome, and its dysregulation is implicated in nearly 70% of human cancers. Although its activity is primarily governed by competition for dimerization partners and occupancy of shared DNA target sequences, the molecular mechanisms controlling oligomerization and DNA binding remain elusive. Here, we employed total protein synthesis and combinatorial assembly to define how posttranslational modification (PTM) patterns regulate the Myc–Max–Mad TF network.

title: Optimization of Sodium-Catalyzed Si–N Bond Formation Through a Comparative Study of Group 1 Alkoxides
abstract: A systematic comparison of group 1 tert-amylate (OtAmyl) salts as precatalysts for Si–N heterodehydrocoupling is reported with a focus on NatOAmyl. The heavier alkali metals provide good to excellent conversions with all substrates screened, including tertiary silanes and secondary amines, which are challenging substrates in prior literature reports. Although the activity of NatOAmyl is limited in comparison to rubidium and cesium congeners, this can be improved with judicious solvent choice, particularly DMSO.

title: Birefringence Breaks Symmetry-Protected Fluorescence Trapping in Laser-Cooled Crystals
abstract: Total internal reflection traps light inside high-index emitters, and in laser-cooled crystals the trapped fluorescence limits how far purification lowers the parasitic heat load. The symmetry of the crystal shape is known to govern this trapping. Here we show that the dielectric tensor supplies a second, intrinsic symmetry, and we unify the geometric and dielectric symmetries in a single conservation law. A fluorescence photon stays trapped when every facet operation conserves a wave-vector component that keeps it inside total internal reflection.

title: Designing organic photoredox catalysts as a fragment-based puzzle solved by reinforcement learning
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) is a promising strategy for identifying optimal solutions in vast search spaces. We have developed a framework in which the design of organic photoredox catalysts (OPCs) is deliberately formulated as a fragment-based puzzle that is well suited to RL. In this framework, an RL agent sequentially selects and orders molecular fragments and attempts to identify fragment combinations that afford high rewards, as calculated based on the similarity between the properties of the generated molecules and those of 4CzIPN, a well-known OPC.

title: Probing Benzoxazine Dimer Formation Using Methyl-Blocked Derivatives as Mechanistic Probes
abstract: The early-stage dimer formation of 1,3-benzoxazine (PH-a) was investigated as a diagnostic system for understanding the ring-opening polymerization (ROP) mechanism using a coupled FAIMS-IRMPD-MS/MS platform. High-field asymmetric waveform ion mobility spectrometry (FAIMS) resolved the protonated PH-a dimer into three distinct populations. A series of methyl-blocked benzoxazine derivatives was used to systematically eliminate individual reactive sites and assign each FAIMS population to a specific reaction route via tandem MS fragmentation patterns and IRMPD action spectroscopy, supported by…

title: Multinotch Isolation Enables Efficient Native Top-down Mass Spectrometry of Proteins in Complex Mixtures.
abstract: Accurate identification of intact proteoforms and their complexes directly from heterogenous biological samples is essential to understand their role in health and disease. While native top-down mass spectrometry (nTDMS) workflows enable this, the extreme molecular complexity of biological samples inadvertently results in overlapping signals which confounds protein identification. One approach to resolving this complexity is gas-phase ion-ion reactions which separate analytical targets according to their original charge state.

title: Cation Mixing Controls Photocatalytic Activity of Ionic Carbon Nitrides by Switching Exciton Character and Electron Localization
An Annotation Consistency Checker for Evidence-Based Evaluation of Untargeted LC-MS/MS Metabolite Annotations
abstract: Untargeted LC-MS/MS metabolomics routinely produces complex annotation landscapes in which individual spectra can yield multiple candidate metabolite annotations. Although spectral similarity provides an essential foundation for library-based annotation, determining whether a candidate annotation is consistent with the available evidence and whether alternative explanations remain plausible requires integration of multiple lines of evidence. In current practice, this evaluation is largely embedded in expert judgment, making annotation review difficult to teach, standardize, and reproduce.

title: Multi-fidelity machine learning interatomic potential for the energetics and finite temperature structure of Pt surfaces and nanoparticles
abstract: Accurate accounting of exposed facets and surface sites is central to understanding metal nanoparticle catalysts, but modelling their structure at finite temperatures is computationally expensive. We benchmark the universal interatomic potential UMA (Universal Model for Atoms, Open Catalyst 2020 task) against Perdew-Burke-Ernzerhof density functional theory (PBE-DFT) for Pt. UMA underestimates the surface energies of all 13 facets by 11-17 % and the excess energies of 28 differently shaped nanoparticles, each containing less than 500 atoms, most strongly for small particles.

title: Coordination-Insertion Copolymerization of Norbornene with α-Olefins using Half-Titanocene Phosphinimide Catalyst
abstract: We previously reported the controlled coordination-insertion polymerization of 2-norbornene (NB) and 5-alkyl-2-norbornenes using a phosphinimide-ligated half-titanocene catalyst (1), affording high-molecular-weight polymers. In this study, the copolymerization of NB with α-olefins, including 1-octene (2), 1-octadecene (3), and 10-undecen-1-ol (4), was investigated to explore the monomer scope and functional group tolerance. Copolymers with Mn values ranging from 2.0 to 20 kg/mol were obtained in moderate to high yields. NB was consumed more rapidly than 2.

title: On the impact of methodological configurations and data variations on chemical recycling life cycle assessment studies
abstract: The comparability of Life Cycle Assessment studies on chemical recycling processes for plastic waste conversion is challenging due to the wide range of investigated feedstocks, datasets, and methodological choices. Thus, this paper investigates the impact of various degrees of freedom within peer-reviewed Life Cycle Assessments of chemical recycling processes on the proposed environmental impact.

title: Origin of the Difference between Kohn-Sham and ∆SCF Band gaps for Delocalized Electron–Hole Excitations in Hybrid-Functional Supercell Calculations
abstract: We examine the relationship between ground-state generalized Kohn–Sham (GKS) band gaps and self-consistent ∆SCF excitation energies for delocalized electron–hole excitations in finite periodic supercells. For a vertical excitation at the undistorted ground-state geometry, these two quantities are expected to coincide when the promoted electron and hole remain Bloch-like. This is mostly true with semilocal functionals, but not with hybrid functionals for which the difference increases linearly with the fraction of exact exchange.

title: Structural Description of Two-Dimensional Nanoscale Networks Using Graph Theory and Graph Growth Algorithms
abstract: Nanostructured networks stand out among other nanostructures for their unique combinations of properties and easily scalable energy-efficient synthesis. Their structural organization is, however, difficult to describe using traditional approaches based on crystallinity. Although revealing distinct structural patterns, the nanoscale networks also have a substantial degree of randomness. Two-dimensional (2D) nanostructured networks self-assembled from nanoparticles present a unique opportunity to develop the methodology for structural description of such materials.

title: An Evidence-Graded Framework for Pharmaceutical Route Selection and Process-Risk Prioritization: A PN6047 Case Study
abstract: Purpose: To develop and demonstrate an evidence-graded framework for screening discovery-scale synthetic routes before experimental process development, using the publicly disclosed route to PN6047, a clinical-stage δ-opioid receptor agonist, as a case study. Methods: No synthesis was performed. Operations exemplified in two patent documents were inventoried; each transformation and its conditions were graded A–D by the strength of public evidence; documented regulatory and hazard attributes were flagged; two process-oriented variants were screened by step count, flags and an…

title: Designing Alloying Interlayers for Metal Anodes in Batteries: Does Nanostructuring Improve Reversibility?
abstract: Metal anodes have been extensively explored as candidates for high-energy rechargeable batteries. However, uncontrolled electrodeposition of metals such as Zn often produces porous, disconnected “dead” metal that limits reversibility. A common mitigation strategy is to introduce an alloying functional layer, which is in general assumed to perform better when nanostructured due to its increased specific surface area and the diffusion scaling relation 𝜏~ 𝐿 2 𝐷 ⁄ .

title: Temperature-dependent Hydrocarbon Chain Packing in Fatty Acid Protocell Membranes at Mineral Interfaces
abstract: Fatty acid vesicles generated through water-rock interactions have been proposed as plausible models of protocells on early Earth. However, how mineral surfaces influence membrane properties over a wide range of temperatures remains unclear. Here, we investigate the temperature-dependent phase transition and hydrocarbon chain packing of vesicles composed of decanoic acid (DA) and 1-decanol (DOH) in contact with FeS, a key hydrothermal vent mineral.

title: Predicting Water-Induced Demixing of Ionic Liquid Mixtures with Associative Electrolyte PC-SAFT
abstract: Ionic liquids (ILs) can be mixed with other ILs to fine-tune their physicochemical properties. While ILs have been long considered inseparable, recent studies have demonstrated that the controlled addition of water enables the selective recovery of the constituent salts, opening new opportunities for sustainable IL recycling and separation. The rational design of these IL mixtures remains challenging due to the lack of predictive models capable of accurately capturing the interplay between competing short- and long-range interactions in IL-based systems, particularly in multi-IL systems…

title: High-Sensitivity, Dual Ratiometric and Turn-on ABATaRs for Multiplexed Temporal Imaging of Ferroptosis Hallmarks in Living Cells
abstract: We present a computationally-guided workflow for designing dual turn-on and ratiometric Raman sensors. The workflow has been used to rationally design activity-based alkyne tagged Raman, ABATaR , sensors that overcome the inherently low Raman sensitivity via strategic placement of electron-donating and electron-withdrawing groups. An ABATaR sensing scaffold designed via the workflow afforded ~ 9000 times higher Raman scattering cross-section than the dimethylsulfoxide C-H stretching-mode.

title: Automated Extraction and FAIRification of Chemical Structures from Scientific Publications
abstract: Chemical structures are published predominantly as images, which makes them inaccessible for database indexing, structure-based search and computational reuse. While Optical Chemical Structure Recognition and PDF-extraction tools attempt post-publication recovery, they cannot restore the information lost during image rendering. To address this, we present BChemXtract, an open-source Java library that extracts chemical structures directly from the CDX and CDXML files that authors already submit with their manuscripts.

title: Group-aware validation sharply reduces the apparent accuracy of extraction-category classification in public cannabis laboratory data
abstract: Published models that classify cannabis products from cannabinoid and terpene profiles report near-perfect accuracy: above 95% for resin type, 100% for chemovar class. These figures come from random cross-validation or Kennard-Stone partitioning, which hold out no plant, producer or laboratory. We quantify the cost on a task with explicit group structure. On 33,229 public laboratory-result rows for cannabis concentrates that name a producer, nearly all from Nevada, each with a source-declared extraction category (non-solvent against solvent-based), a gradient-boosted classifier scores 78.5%…

title: Paper2CIF: An AI Agent for Reconstructing Atomistic Models to Discover Structure-Reactivity Relationships
abstract: Reinterpreting published chemical findings requires explicit atomic structures that connect experimental observations with reactivity. Here we report Paper2CIF, an artificial intelligence (AI) agent that reconstructs sample-specific atomic structures from published chemical evidence for structure-reactivity relationship investigations. Across 171 interdisciplinary articles, Paper2CIF achieves 97.08% phase identification accuracy and 91.23% final structural accuracy, with correct structures satisfying all applicable reported constraints, including composition, site occupancy, and local…

title: Tyr10 Modifications and Peptide Context Rewire GLP-1 Modulation of Amyloid-β42 Assembly
abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) is best known as a receptor agonist, yet its peptide-level behavior in protein-rich environments remains poorly defined. Here, a GLP-1-directed photoaffinity probe recovered a predefined Aβ42 spike-in from cell lysates, while endogenous actin and α-synuclein were detected in the recovered fractions. This observation motivated chemically defined assembly studies with the actinlinked β-thymosin reference TMSB4Y. Thioflavin T (ThT) kinetics and endpoint electron microscopy (EM) revealed no single pro- or antiassembly response.

title: Unveiling Photoluminescent N-Heterocyclic Silylene-Silver(I) Amides as Dual-Function Photosensitizers and Third-Harmonic Generators
abstract: N-Heterocyclic silylenes (NHSis) have evolved from laboratory curiosities to versatile ligands for small-molecule activation and homogeneous catalysis, yet their potential in photophysics and optical materials remains unexplored. Here, we report for the first time a series of luminescent NHSi-ligated Ag(I) amide complexes (2–4) exhibiting remarkable thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) and dual-emissive behavior.

title: Metal-Free Photoinduced Divergent Activation of N2O and H2 Employing Main-Group Radical Pairs
abstract: Activating robust small molecules like nitrous oxide (N2O) and molecular hydrogen (H2) without transition metals is a key challenge in sustainable chemistry. To address this, we developed an efficient photochemical platform that uses silylphosphanes to divergently activate both the gases. Under photoirradiation, the silylphosphane’s P-Si bond undergoes rapid homolytic cleavage, releasing highly reactive silyl and phosphinyl radicals.

title: Mechanochemical nitrogen fixation into amides and nitriles.
Hydrogenolysis of N-Cbz-Protected Amines Mediated by Spherical SiliaCat Pd(0)
abstract: The deprotection reaction of N-benzyloxycarbonyl (N-Cbz)-protected amino groups in organic compounds can be efficiently achieved by hydrogenolysis mediated by the sol-gel-entrapped spherical catalyst SiliaCat Pd(0). The heterogeneous catalyst combines high catalytic activity and chemoselectivity with low Pd loading, a nonpyrophoric nature, and excellent reusability.

title: Tracking Surface Charge of Gold Single-Crystal Electrodes with Diffuse Layer Force Microscopy
abstract: Electrochemistry is a powerful approach for the interconversion of electrical and chemical energy. This is enabled by the nanoscale confined potential difference occurring at an interface, such as that between a solid and a liquid. As such, the structure of this region of separated charge, or electrical double layer, inherently includes molecular scale ordering in the liquid, as well as atomic scale details of the electrode, making it challenging to obtain a detailed picture of the potential-dependent state of electrochemical interfaces.

title: Aza-Michael Addition of Aliphatic Amines to Weakly Polarised Alkenes via Organobase Catalysis
abstract: The direct addition of aliphatic amines to alkenes offers an atom-economical route to valuable N-alkyl amines, but remains challenging for weakly polarised alkenes. This is because C–N bond formation is poorly driven thermodynamically and difficult to achieve without strongly activating the alkene or generating more reactive nitrogen species. Here we report an organobase-catalysed strategy that enables anti-Markovnikov addition of secondary aliphatic amines to weakly polarised (hetero)aryl alkenes.

title: A species-resolved well-balanced lattice Boltzmann framework for Maxwell–Stefan diffusion in non-ideal multiphase multicomponent transport
abstract: Simulating non-ideal multiphase multicomponent transport requires coupled solution of phase equilibrium, hydrodynamics, and multicomponent diffusion. Recent thermodynamically consistent and well-balanced lattice Boltzmann formulations have addressed multiphase equilibria, but their integration with multicomponent diffusion is less developed. In this work, a speciesresolved well-balanced lattice Boltzmann framework is developed to incorporate Maxwell–Stefan diffusion into non-ideal multiphase multicomponent transport.

title: GMAP: A General Purpose Hamiltonian Mapping Program for Computational Spectroscopy
abstract: Vibrational and electronic spectra provide useful information about structure, dynamics, and function in the condensed phase. Electrostatic mappings have proved to be powerful tools for predicting and interpreting both vibrational and electronic spectra. Numerous special purpose programs exist; however, a general purpose framework is still missing. In this paper, we present a new general purpose mapping program for bridging the gap between structural and dynamical information obtained in molecular dynamics simulations and programs for calculating spectroscopic observables.

title: Aerobic ethanol oxidation by magnetic inductive heating of Pd NPs supported onto Ni foam
abstract: Selective aerobic oxidation of ethanol to acetic acid is an attractive example of the conversion of biomass-derived alcohol value-added chemicals. In this context, conventional liquidphase processes often rely on harsh conditions, long reaction times, inefficient external heating and limited catalyst recovery. Herein, a radically new strategy for acetic acid synthesis from ethanol is proposed and demonstrated. The catalyst used is designed not only as the active phase for chemical transformation, but also as the element responsible for local heat generation.

title: Pd-catalyzed Cycloadditions of 5-Vinyloxazolidine-2,4-diones: A Diastereo- and Enantioselective Access to Spirooxindoles
abstract: In this manuscript, we report a straightforward route to spirooxindoles by Pd-catalyzed cycloadditions of 5-vinyloxazolidine-2,4-diones with isatins. After a screening of chiral ligands, DTBM-SEGPHOS was selected to induce high diastereo- and enantiocontrol of the two newly created tetrasubstituted stereocenters. Our investigation demonstrated broad functional group tolerance under the reaction conditions. Overall, this work represents a rare example of Pd-catalyzed cycloadditions involving 5- vinyloxazolidine-2,4-diones and electrophilic C=O bonds.

title: Memory-Augmented Generative Design of Octahedral Co(II) Complexes with Targeted Zero-Field Splitting
abstract: The discovery of coordination complexes with targeted magnetic anisotropy remains challenging because the enormous chemical space of ligands and coordination environments makes propertydirected molecular design difficult to achieve by conventional screening. Here, we introduce a memoryaugmented generative framework for the inverse design of octahedral Co(II) complexes with targeted zero-field splitting (ZFS). A chemically curated dataset of ~6000 Co(II) complexes, was used to establish a broad electronic-structure landscape spanning positive and negative ZFS regimes.

title: Composition-Dependent Remodeling of the ABCB1Disordered Linker by Plasma-Generated ReactiveMixtures
abstract: Multidrug resistance (MDR) mediated by the efflux transporter ABCB1 (P-glycoprotein) remains a major barrier in cancer chemotherapy. Because classical active-site inhibitors have largely failed clinically due to off-target toxicity, disrupting the interdomain mechanical coupling required for transport has emerged as an attractive alternative. Cold atmospheric plasma (CAP) generates coexisting reactive oxygen and nitrogen species (RONS) capable of sensitizing chemoresistant cells, yet how multicomponent reactive mixtures dynamically perturb the intrinsically disordered NBD1–TMD2 linker, a…

title: A Solution-Gated Graphene Transistor Sensor for the Detection and Quantification of Guanine Quadruplexes.
abstract: SGGT G4 Detection 2 ABSTRACT. We report the design, realization, and testing of a Solution-Gated Graphene Transistor Sensor aimed at detecting and quantifying guanine quadruplexes. By using all-atom molecular dynamic simulations complemented with free energy methods we rationally design the architecture of the sensors, exploiting an economic and easy-available G4 ligand. The prototype of the sensor has shown the capacity to provide a linear response depending on the G4 concentration, hence showing the proof of concept of its applicability for G4 detection.

title: A soluble conductive chromium coordination polymer with radical ligands and non-integer redox states
abstract: There are few conductive metal-organic materials that are solution processible or that feature electron-accepting conductive units. Thus, a soluble, semiconductive coordination polymer (1n+)x (n = 1 – 3) was developed by linking CrIII ions with electron-deficient back-to-back bis-terpyridine (btpy) ligands. CrIII promotes reduction of these ligands under mild conditions (starting at −0.16 V vs. Fc+/0), providing the first extended material with btpy•− or btpy2− units.

title: Chemically modified hydrogels to improve geothermal reservoir performance by enabling flow control via size-shifting microspheres
abstract: Thermal short circuits, where fluids preferentially connect injection and production wells, are a leading cause of premature enthalpy decline in geothermal reservoirs. These pathways accelerate cooling, reduce effective heat transfer area, and limit reservoir lifetime. We propose a temperature-responsive hydrogel microsphere suspension as an “active tracer” that dynamically redirects flow away from cooled short-circuit channels while also tracing fluid flow via fluorescence spectroscopy.

title: VISION-BASED DRY-MATERIAL INVENTORY ESTIMATION IN AUTONOMOUS LABORATORIES: RGB SEGMENTATION VERSUS RGB-D SURFACE RECONSTRUCTION
abstract: Reliable dry-material inventory monitoring is needed for autonomous laboratory operation, but the suitability of a non-contact method depends on material behaviour, optical access, calibration requirements and the quantity to be estimated. We compared two vision-based approaches—material-specific RGB/YOLO level estimation and visible-surface reconstruction from an Intel RealSense D405—across three materials (black polypropylene pellets, wood powder, and microcrystalline cellulose fine powder) in small transparent laboratory tubes representative of common dosing instruments, with the aim of…

title: Bio-derived ionic conductive Guar Gum hydrogels as distributed circuit elements for analogue signal processing: the case of Resistor-Capacitor filters
abstract: Developing functional electronic materials from renewable resources is a key challenge toward more sustainable electronics. Here, we report on a bio-derived ionic conductive hydrogel based on guar gum and demonstrate its direct integration as a functional circuit element for analogue signal processing. Ionic conductivity is introduced by incorporating sodium chloride into the polysaccharide matrix and systematically tuned through the glycerol and salt contents.

title: Process and Systems Modeling of Hydrothermal Liquefaction for Fuels and
abstract: 17 Hydrothermal liquefaction (HTL) can convert wet organic waste into fuels and bioproducts, but 18 variation in feedstocks and operating conditions can propagate from product yields to system 19 performance and deployment. This study linked machine learning based HTL yield prediction with 20 process simulation, techno-economic analysis (TEA), life cycle assessment (LCA), uncertainty 21 analysis, and surrogate modeling. A literature data set of 402 experiments was used to predict 22 biocrude, aqueous, gas, and solids yields, with 71.8% of predictions within ±5 wt% of experimental 23 values.

title: Predictive Model for Acid-Catalyzed SN1 Solvolysis Racemization of Chiral Alcohols in Water
abstract: We have developed a predictive model for assessing the racemization risk of drug candidates featuring chiral alcohol motifs, addressing an important concern in drug discovery and development. Specifically, it predicts the activation free energy of stereoisomerization through the acid-catalyzed SN1 solvolysis mechanism based on the calculated electronic reaction energy associated with carbocation formation, the assumed rate-determining step.

title: A Redox-Non-Innocent Catecholate Shifts the Oxidation State Break in the Actinides
abstract: Realizing the full potential of actinide-based systems requires strategies to differentiate elements whose similar chemical properties complicate their selective use. Redox-active ligands offer a promising approach: their ability to participate in electron transfer provides a means to tune the oxidation states and electronic structures of both lanthanides and actinides. To explore this approach, we conducted a theory-guided study of (Tp*)2An(dtbsq) complexes (1-An; An = U, Np, Pu, Am, Bk; Tp* = [HB(C3N2Me2H)3]-; dtbsq•− = [C6O2 tBu2H2]-), which contain a redox-active semiquinone ligand.

title: Machine Learning of Methacrylated Dextran Phase Separation for Prediction, Transferability, and Adaptation
abstract: Thermoresponsive polymers are promising materials for separations, sensing, drug delivery, and other biomedical applications, but their phase behavior depends on numerous polymer and solution variables, which creates a formulation space that is impractical to explore exhaustively by experiments. Here, we develop machine-learning (ML) models for predicting the lower critical solution temperature (LCST) of methacrylated dextran (Dex-MA), a biocompatible polysaccharide-based polymer, using 403 unique experimentally measured formulations spanning polymer molecular weight, degree of…

title: Structural Insights into the Expanded Substrate Scope of a Cysteine-Dependent Hydrolase from Rhodococcus opacus for Polyethylene, Polypropylene, and Polystyrene Biodegradation
abstract: Microplastic pollution from homopolymers such as polypropylene (PP), polystyrene (PS), and polyethylene (PE) poses growing health and environmental concerns, highlighting the need for robust polymer-degrading biocatalysts. We previously identified a naturally occurring cysteine-dependent hydrolase (CsdH) from Rhodococcus opacus, featuring a unique Cys160-Lys127-Asp39 catalytic triad and providing a novel mechanism for polyethylene terephthalate (PET) degradation. In this study, we have determined crystal structures of CsdH in complex with PP, PS, PE, and styrene and demonstrated the potential of the enzyme to directly degrade these homopolymers into their respective low molecular weight degradation products using LC-MS. Structural analysis reveals that the enzyme retains a conserved principal access tunnel while undergoing subtle substrate-dependent changes to accommodate different substrates. The enzyme exhibited broad plastic degradation activity with the highest weight loss observed for PE, followed by PP and PS. SEM analysis reveals surface roughness, cracks and grooves, confirming polymer degradation. Further, these results corroborate through FTIR and TGA analysis. These findings establish a strong foundation for enzyme engineering and aim at developing efficient microplastic degradation.

title: Aging Differentially Remodels the Retina and RPE/Choroid Proteome and Metabolism
abstract: Purpose: The neural retina and retinal pigment epithelium/choroid (RPE/Cho) are metabolically coupled. Metabolic dysfunction of the RPE/Cho contributes to photoreceptor death in age-related macular degeneration (AMD). This study aimed to determine how aging, a major risk factor for AMD, alters the proteome and metabolic pathways in the retina and RPE/Cho. Methods: We performed quantitative proteomics on neural retina and RPE/Cho from young (8-week) and old (73-week) C57BL/6J mice. The differentially expressed proteins between old and young, as well as between the retina and RPE/Cho, were visualized using volcano plots and heatmaps, and functional analyses were assessed by Gene Ontology enrichment tools. Results: Aging altered the expression of 85 retinal proteins and 272 RPE/Cho, with 16 shared between tissues. In the aged retina, proteins associated with NADP(H) metabolism, neurodegeneration, and immunity were mostly upregulated, while proteins in lipid metabolism, transcription, and epigenetic regulation decreased. In the aged RPE/Cho, all 21 significantly altered lysosomal enzymes and transport proteins increased, together with complement components, and photoreceptor outer segment proteins. These changes accompanied increases in proteins associated with lipid metabolism and protection against lipid peroxidation, while several glutathione metabolism enzymes decreased. Seven shared proteins involved in lipid and NADP(H) metabolism, changed in opposite directions between retina and RPE/Cho. Comparison of the retinal and RPE/Cho proteomes identified 3073 differentially abundant proteins, of which 2452 maintained tissue-specific differences across both age groups, while approximately 17% showed age-dependent shifts in tissue enrichment. These shifts involved proteins associated with metabolism, extracellular matrix, visual function, lysosomal pathways, and innate immunity. Within the metabolic proteome, several glycolytic and fatty acid oxidation proteins showed greater relative enrichment in RPE/Cho with age, whereas glucose transporters and mitochondrial complexes shifted toward the retina. Conclusions: Overall, these findings show that aging differentially remodels the retina and RPE/Cho proteome, accompanied by altered metabolic specialization between the two tissues.

title: STRUCTURAL AND MOLECULAR DYNAMICS ANALYSIS OF HUMAN β-DEFENSIN 1 VARIANTS REVEALS DISTINCT PERTURBATION SIGNATURES
abstract: Human {beta}-defensin 1 (hBD-1) is a small, disulfide-constrained antimicrobial peptide produced predominantly in the kidney and urogenital tract, where it contributes to epithelial innate defense. Genetic variation in the gene encoding hBD-1 has been associated with altered expression levels and susceptibility to infections, including infection following solid organ transplantation, yet the molecular consequences of coding substitutions in the active, mature form remain largely undefined.

title: CryoFAST: A Fab-Aided Cryo-EM Workflow for High-Resolution Structure Determination of Sub-50-kDa Protein Targets
abstract: Single-particle cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) plays an increasingly important role in structure-based drug discovery (SBDD) by revealing target protein-ligand interactions at the molecular level, but its application has largely focused on large- and medium-sized protein complexes. Many therapeutically important targets are smaller than 50 kDa and remain highly challenging for cryo-EM analysis because of low signal-to-noise ratios and difficulties in particle alignment. Here, we describe cryoFAST, an integrated workflow that couples ligand-compatible Fab discovery and structure-guided computational maturation with biochemical triage, fiducial-complex assembly, and single-particle cryo-EM. Through phage-display screening and/or AI-guided design, we developed high-affinity Fab binders of approximately 50 kDa that stabilize the target without disrupting ligand-target interactions and then assembled Fab-target complexes for cryo-EM analysis. Using the therapeutically relevant extracellular domain (~20 kDa) of interleukin-4 receptor (IL-4R) as a proof of concept, we determined its cryo-EM structure at 2.74 Angstrom resolution and established a framework for elucidating ligand-binding modes. This workflow provides a practical, efficient, and potentially broadly applicable route to the structural characterization of small protein targets that are otherwise challenging to study. By extending the applicability of cryo-EM to high-value but technically challenging small targets, cryoFAST may open new opportunities for structure-based drug discovery.

title: The Batten disease gene product CLN6 is a glycerophosphoglycerol epimerase that establishes S,S-BMP stereochemistry
abstract: Bis(monoacylglycero)phosphate (BMP), a lysosomal phospholipid essential for lipid catabolism and cholesterol clearance, has a noncanonical S,S glycerol configuration found in no other mammalian phospholipid, a feature necessary for its stability in the lysosome. How cells invert glycerol stereochemistry to build S,S-BMP has remained unexplained since this configuration was discovered five decades ago. Here, we show that the endoplasmic reticulum-resident Batten disease protein CLN6 is a Ca2+-dependent epimerase that isomerizes glycerophosphoglycerol (GPG) from R,S-GPG to S,S-GPG. CLN6-deficient cells, mouse tissues, and patient samples predominantly contain R,S-GPG, S,R-lysophosphatidylglycerol (LPG), and R,S-BMP instead of their S,S counterparts, with a net depletion of BMP. Purified CLN6 catalyzes GPG epimerization in vitro, an activity abolished by a pathogenic substitution in its substrate-binding pocket. Consistently, exogenous S,S-GPG restores BMP synthesis and relieves lipid storage in CLN6-null cells. Our work establishes stereochemical commitment upstream of acylation, placing CLN6, CLN8, and CLN5 in sequence in BMP biosynthesis and unifying the lipid defect across these neurodegenerative disorders.

title: Sense-and-response to intracellular signaling via nucleocytoplasmic localization control of a synthetic transcription factor platform
abstract: Many therapeutically relevant signaling pathways are sensed inside the cell, yet a modular synthetic biology platform for responding to intracellular signaling at the post-translational level is lacking. Signaling pathways control the nuclear localization and activity of native transcription factors via phosphorylation of nuclear localization/export or cytoplasmic anchor sequences.

title: Advancing chemical reaction prediction in data-scarce drug discovery with active and geometric deep learning
abstract: The success of generative molecular design depends on the synthetic accessibility of the molecules it creates. While computational models can help predict chemical reactions, their current effectiveness is limited by a lack of reference data and the difficulty of accurately predicting reaction regioselectivity. Here, to address this, we present an integrated closed-loop workflow that combines efficient reaction data acquisition with high-accuracy deep learning. We developed an active learning strategy, driven by a tree-based ensemble, to guide the acquisition of the most informative laboratory experiments. This experimental campaign yielded a diverse benchmark for C–H borylation. The bespoke dataset allowed us to train and evaluate geometric graph neural networks. We demonstrate that augmenting these symmetry-aware models with self-supervised auxiliary tasks consistently improves performance for both reaction outcome prediction and regioselectivity prediction. Prospective tests on unseen substrates, featuring challenging N -heteroaryl motifs, pinpointed the correct borylation positions in all cases, illustrating the practical utility of our workflow for efficient drug optimization.

title: A transient third metal ion shapes the catalytic cycle of a group I intron ribozyme
abstract: The self-splicing group I intron ribozyme from Tetrahymena thermophillia (THr) is a prototypical example of how RNA overcomes its limited chemical repertoire to form complex, negatively charged junctions and catalyze chemical reactions. Despite over 30 years of biochemical and structural characterization, questions still remain regarding the requirements for THr catalysis that may inform structure based drug design against group I introns, as well as the use of THr as an RNA editing tool. Recent cryo-EM structures have provided an unprecedented window into the first and second steps of splicing, enabling detailed mechanistic investigation at the atomistic level. In this work, we leverage solvation theory, molecular dynamics, alchemical free energy simulations, and machine learning accelerated QM/MM to probe outstanding questions related to 1) the role of a possible third Mg2+ binding in the active site, 2) differences in catalytic requirements between Gexo cofactors and between the first and second steps of splicing, 3) the potential role of an acid or base, and 4) restrictions on the identity of the 5' exon splice site nucleotide, U(-1). We propose that a transient, cofactor dependent, interaction with a third metal participates in the first step, while a higher affinity interaction with this third ion is required in the second step. We also propose that the presence of a phosphate on the Gexo in the first step, and analogously the G{omega} in the second step, forms a metal ion binding site not present when guanosine is bound. Finally, we propose and computationally test design modifications of G22 (isofunctional substitutions of 2,6-diaminopurine that tune the pKa at the N1 position) that we predict will enable the accommodation of C(-1) in a crucial wobble-like pair at physiological pH. This design would provide a potential strategy for expanding the sequence space accessible to programmable trans-splicing ribozymes in RNA editing applications.

title: CLN6 is a glycerophosphoglycerol epimerase in bis(monoacylglycero)phosphate biosynthesis
abstract: Lysosomal catabolism depends on bis(monoacylglycero)phosphate (BMP), a phospholipid with atypical S,S stereochemistry of unknown biosynthetic origin. CLN8 and CLN5 catalyze sequential acylation steps in BMP synthesis, and their loss of function causes Batten disease, a group of inherited neurodegenerative lysosomal storage disorders. Here we identify CLN6, a biochemically uncharacterized endoplasmic reticulum protein whose loss also causes Batten disease, as the calcium-dependent glycerophosphoglycerol epimerase that establishes BMP stereochemistry upstream of CLN8. CLN6 deficiency depletes BMP in cells, mice, and patient lysosomes, and reduces lysosomal hydrolase levels. BMP-precursor supplementation bypasses CLN6, restores BMP and increases hydrolase abundance in CLN6-deficient cells and mice. These findings place three Batten disease proteins in a single biosynthetic pathway and reveal BMP deficiency as a reversible cause of disrupted lysosomal hydrolase homeostasis.

title: Photobiocatalytic Diastereo- and Enantioselective Synthesis of Non-Canonical Amino Acids Bearing Challenging Stereochemical Dyads and Triads
abstract: Catalyst-controlled stereodivergent synthesis of acyclic molecules bearing multiple stereogenic centers remains a longstanding challenge in asymmetric catalysis, particularly through intermolecular radical C-C coupling. Here, we report the directed evolution of pyridoxal 5'-phosphate (PLP)-dependent biocatalysts for the stereodivergent synthesis of non canonical amino acids bearing either skipped , {gamma}-stereochemical dyads or contiguous , {beta}, {gamma}-stereochemical triads. Starting from a thermophilic tryptophan synthase {beta}-subunit, protein engineering generated complementary enzyme variants that selectively construct three of the four possible , {gamma}-stereoisomers through biocatalyst-controlled reversal of both remote {gamma}-stereochemistry and proximal -stereochemistry. These engineered enzymes catalyzed intermolecular radical C-C bond formation with a broad range of secondary alkyltrifluoroborates, affording , {gamma}-disubstituted amino acids in excellent yields and stereoselectivities. Furthermore, directed evolution enabled efficient {beta}-dehydroxylative radical coupling of the non-native threonine-derived aminoacrylate intermediate, providing amino acids bearing contiguous , {beta}, {gamma}-stereochemical triads with up to 96:4:99:1 e.r.. To further demonstrate the synthetic utility of this platform, the stereochemically enriched amino acids were transformed into valuable {gamma}-chiral amines through engineered PLP dependent tryptophan decarboxylases, establishing a dual PLP enzyme based biocatalytic cascade for the enantiodivergent synthesis of privileged amine scaffolds. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that enzyme controlled {gamma}-stereoselectivity originates from active-site remodeling that modulates {pi}-{pi} interactions and steric contacts governing the facial selectivity of the radical addition step. This work expands the synthetic capabilities of radical biocatalysis by enabling catalyst-controlled stereodivergent assembly of complex acyclic stereochemical arrays and establishes engineered PLP enzymes as versatile catalysts for the synthesis of stereochemically complex amino acids and chiral amines.

title: Direct visualization of lysosome-mediated intracellular transport and membrane anchoring of TNF-α in human T cells
abstract: Tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-) represents a major pro-inflammatory cytokine associated with chronic inflammation. Enhanced understanding of intracellular trafficking of TNF- enables the identification of drug targets that modulate TNF- secretion at the cellular source. However, conventional cytokine assays provide only bulk measurements of secreted TNF- or static measurements in fixed cells and therefore cannot provide mechanistic information. Here, we report a fluorescence imaging platform to visualize and quantify intracellular TNF- trafficking in human T cells. Using a Jurkat T cell line stably expressing TNF- fused to mStayGold as a model system, we revealed through single-particle tracking (SPT) that T cell activation increased the motility of TNF- vesicles and that microtubule perturbation disrupted this increased motility. 3D structured illumination microscopy uncovered spatial associations between TNF- vesicles and lysosomes, and SPT further demonstrated their coordinated transport. Using total internal reflection fluorescence microscopy, we captured the sub-second splitting of single TNF- vesicles into multiple puncta that subsequently separated, suggesting delivery of TNF- from the vesicle to the plasma membrane. Confocal-based super-resolution microscopy further resolved TNF- vesicles fusing with the plasma membrane and transmembrane TNF-. Together, these imaging capabilities for tracking and super-resolving the intracellular transport and membrane delivery of TNF- in live T cells enable mechanistic studies of TNF- trafficking and release.

title: Fusion Peptide Insertion Configuration Determines the Mechanism of Membrane Curvature Induction in Human Parainfluenza Virus Type 3
abstract: Viral entry requires remodeling the host membrane with a short fusion peptide (FP) that anchors and deforms the target lipid bilayer. However, the contribution of the FP throughout the full fusion pathway remains unknown. Here, all-atom molecular dynamics simulations define the membrane- deformation mechanisms associated with two distinct insertion configurations of membrane-bound human parainfluenza virus type 3 (HPIV3) FP. Molecular simulations quantifying the linear response of curvature to the peptide are complemented with analyses of lipid organization and FP-lipid interactions to define the underlying membrane-deformation mechanisms. The surface-parallel FP configuration generates positive membrane curvature through deformation of the proximal leaflet, consistent with the classical hydrophobic insertion (wedging) mechanism. In contrast, the transmembrane FP configuration generates curvature through localized deformation of the distal leaflet, a distinct mechanism that would strongly influence later stages of fusion. Cryo-electron tomography shows that target membrane curvature at virus-host contact sites is consistent with the molecular dynamics prediction. In the absence of F-protein activation and FP insertion, the cryo-ET-determined curvature distribution shifts toward negative values, thereby isolating the role of the fusion protein in inducing early-stage curvature that enables the host and virus membranes to approach one another. Modeling key mutational changes isolates how aromatic and electrostatic interactions act together to promote curvature generation. Taken together, these findings establish FP insertion configuration as a determinant of productive membrane curvature across the full fusion pathway.

title: X-ray-Triggered Self-Sustaining Afterglow Scaffolds with Persistent Type-I/II ROS Generation for Imaging-Guided Hypoxic Tumor Therapy
abstract: Afterglow imaging-guided photodynamic therapy (PDT) eliminates tissue autofluorescence and enables real-time therapeutic monitoring, yet its efficacy is constrained by shallow light penetration and tumor hypoxia. X-ray activation overcomes the depth barrier, but an integrated platform that simultaneously addresses hypoxia and provides persistent afterglow feedback remains lacking.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Graphene-Like-Armored Nanosheet Assemblies toward Fast and Stable High-Mass-Loading Sodium Storage
abstract: Sodium-ion batteries represent promising energy storage devices, yet their deployment is severely hampered by sluggish ion-transport kinetics and unstable electrode–electrolyte interfacial chemistry that deteriorate rate capability and cycling lifespan, particularly under high-loading electrode configurations. Here, we report a structural anode design comprising double-shelled TiO2 spheres assembled from cross-distributed 2 nm thick nanosheets and uniformly encapsulated by a graphene-like armor.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Physics-Guided Design of Ammonia Decomposition Catalysts with Interpretable Machine Learning
abstract: Rational catalyst design for ammonia decomposition requires navigating coupled structural and electronic effects that govern reaction energetics across a large configurational space. Here, we integrate density functional theory (DFT), microkinetic modeling (MKM), and interpretable machine learning to establish a physics-guided screening framework. For the most active stepped Ru(10–13) surface, MKM identifies NH* dissociation as the rate-limiting step and defines an NH* binding-energy window of -4.47 to -3.84 eV that sustains near-maximal turnover frequency across 673–750 K and applied fields…

title: Potassium modulates Phytophthora zoospore motility and flagellar beating through dose-dependent effects
abstract: Biflagellate zoospores are critical agents in the spread of Phytophthora spp., plant pathogens causing major agronomic and economic losses worldwide. These motile cells navigate soil water films toward plant roots using taxis triggered by environmental cues. Here, we investigate how potassium modulates zoospore motility by analyzing trajectory and flagellar beating parameters across KCl concentrations.

title: Amide I kurtosis maps cardiac amyloid in human tissue by ultrabroadband multiplex coherent anti-Stokes Raman scattering (CARS) microscopy
abstract: Cardiac amyloidosis is caused by deposits of misfolded proteins in the heart and can lead to heart failure. Histological confirmation typically involves staining tissue sections with Congo red and examining them under polarized light for apple-green birefringence; however, achieving an interpretable, label-free, and observer-independent assessment remains challenging. Here we show that Pearson kurtosis of channel intensities within the amide I window provides an interpretable, fitting-free contrast for cardiac amyloid in unstained human cardiac tissue sections from ten participants imaged by ultrabroadband multiplex coherent anti-Stokes Raman scattering (CARS). In a discovery participant, high-kurtosis regions corresponded with Congo red-positive tissue in two CARS-histology pairs of adjacent sections (descriptive spatial AUCs, 0.79 and 0.73). Across 15 fields from nine additional participants, field-level kurtosis values did not overlap between severe-deposition and Congo red-negative tissue fields. Among the descriptors examined, kurtosis showed the largest standardized participant-level separation. Exploratory multivariate curve resolution yielded a deposit-associated component with aromatic-residue features shared with reagent transthyretin. In one field from the discovery participant, the second harmonic generation (SHG) signal, acquired simultaneously with CARS, showed a broadly inverse spatial pattern relative to the amide I kurtosis map, revealing distinct tissue-architectural contrast. Together, these findings support a potential label-free approach to detecting cardiac amyloid deposits that combines amide I kurtosis derived from broadband CARS with SHG-derived architectural contrast.

title: A glycosaminoglycan degrading Polysaccharide Utilization Locus in the oral microbiota species Segatella oris
abstract: The human gut microbiota has been explored for the last two decades and studies have uncovered its major role in the degradation of complex glycans from the diet as well as the host tissues. Strikingly, until very recently, no similar investigation has been carried out on the human oral cavity microbiota, which is increasingly recognized has an important parameter in gastrointestinal health. Prevotellaceae are an important and under-investigated family of bacteria in both the gut and the oral cavity microbiota. The oral cavity is particularly rich in glycosaminoglycans which could provide an abundant carbon source for the inhabiting microorganisms, and play a significant role in host-pathogen interactions. Hence, we analyzed Polysaccharide Utilization Loci in oral microbiota species and we identified a glycosaminoglycan-degrading Polysaccharide Utilization Locus in Segatella oris. We produced and characterized the four enzymes, confirmed their ability to degrade glycosaminoglycans, and we focused our efforts on the biochemical and structural characterization of the first reported Prevotellaceae endosulfatase.

title: Proton-Donor Identity Shapes Electrochemical Nitrate Reduction on Silver
abstract: Electrocatalytic nitrate reduction is a key reaction in nitrogen cycling and water remediation, yet the mechanistic interpretation of its voltammetric response remains poorly understood. On silver electrodes, cyclic voltammograms often display multiple cathodic features assigned to different reaction steps, although a consistent mechanistic interpretation remains elusive. Here, we combine cyclic voltammetry analysis with in situ product detection using scanning electrochemical microscopy (SECM), and hydrodynamic analysis using rotating disk electrode (RDE), to investigate nitrate-to-nitrite electroreduction on silver. We show that the cathodic response changes from a single peak to two distinct features with increasing nitrate concentration when using phosphate buffer as a supporting electrolyte. Analysis of concentration, scan rate, and pH dependencies, together with systematic variation of phosphate electrolyte composition, indicates that these features arise from distinct interfacial proton-transfer regimes associated with the availability of H2PO4– as a proton donor. In addition, SECM enables the assignment of each feature to local nitrite formation, ruling out changes in product identity as the origin of each feature. These findings show that phosphate electrolyte modulates proton-donor availability, and, consequently, the voltammetric response of nitrate reduction on silver, providing a framework for interpreting the complex electrocatalytic behavior observed in this system.

title: Physical Basis Of pKa Shift For Ionizable Lipids In An LNP-like Environment
abstract: Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) are a leading drug delivery platform for mRNA or other nucleic acid-based therapeutics. LNP platforms are typically composed of ionizable aminolipids, phospholipids, sterols, and lipids tagged with polyethylene glycol. The ionizable aminolipids are typically cationic at low pH, allowing them to encapsulate negatively charged mRNA. The pH at which the ionizable head groups change charge states, the apparent pKa, is crucial to understand the characteristics and formulation of LNP. However, this is difficult to measure as the apparent pKa differs from the pKa of the aminolipids in bulk solution due to the complex chemical and charge environment. In this study, we use molecular dynamics (MD) simulations with alchemical free energy perturbation to calculate the pKa shift as a function of lipid composition, treating LNP-like and vesicle-like environments. Our results show that the pH-dependent structure of the systems affects the trends in pKa shifts in complex ways, driven by factors including surface electrostatics and lipid internalization. Our all-atom simulation protocol allows us to efficiently estimate the apparent pKa of LNP-like models formed with novel ionizable aminolipids and estimate how it will change with composition.

title: Iron exposure reprograms redox homeostasis through mitochondrial depolarization in neuroblastoma
abstract: Purpose. Neuroblastoma is the most common malignancy of infancy, and cancer cells strongly depend on iron metabolism for proliferation. Whether sub-cytotoxic iron load reprograms mitochondrial and redox metabolism, and how this relates to the malignant behavior of neuroblastoma cells, is poorly defined. We hypothesized that exposure of human neuroblastoma cells to a non-toxic iron overload perturbs mitochondrial and redox metabolism, thereby affecting cancer cell properties. Methods. SH-SY5Y neuroblastoma cells were exposed to 100 M iron sulfate for 24 h. The resulting changes were monitored using complementary methods, including cell viability, cytotoxicity, proliferation and migration assays, intracellular iron quantification by ICP-MS, confocal imaging of mitochondrial morphology and membrane potential ({Delta}{Psi}m), high-resolution respirometry with flux control ratios, probe-based oxidant and H2O2 measurements, and label-free quantitative proteomics with Ingenuity Pathway Analysis. Results. Non-toxic iron loading raised intracellular iron about four-fold, promoted cell proliferation and reduced migration. Iron induced mitochondrial fragmentation and {Delta}{Psi}m depolarization while preserving mitochondrial content and OXPHOS coupling efficiency. Among respiratory states, only proton-leak respiration increased, paralleled by a higher leak/ETS coupling ratio. Total cellular oxidant levels and H2O2 output were strongly reduced. The proteome showed downregulation of ribosomal proteins and translation/RNA-processing components and upregulation of histones and ferritin. Conclusion. Mild iron exposure reprograms mitochondrial and redox metabolism in neuroblastoma cells. The observed selective increase in proton leak lowers {Delta}{Psi}m to a range that biophysically limits oxidant production while OXPHOS coupling is preserved. Interfering with this adaptive, proton leak-dependent and preventive antioxidant program may offer a way to alter neuroblastoma progression.

title: Multi-source data integration and ensemble machine learning analysis of the role of Corilagin in regulating endoplasmic reticulum stress and alleviating intestinal ischemia reperfusion injury in mice.
abstract: Intestinal ischemia-reperfusion injury (IIRI) is driven by oxidative stress, excessive inflammation, Endoplasmic Reticulum Stress (ERS), and disruption of the intestinal epithelial barrier. Corilagin, a natural ellagitannin with antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities, has shown protective effects against IIRI; however, its cross-species and multitarget mechanisms remain unclear. This study investigated the protective mechanisms of Corilagin against IIRI by integrating Corilagin-related targets, IIRI-associated genes, and an ERS gene set. Differential expression analyses of GSE37013 and GSE96733 were combined with an ensemble machine-learning framework comprising 15 algorithms to prioritize core genes. Molecular docking and 100-ns all-atom molecular dynamics simulations using the AlphaFold-predicted full-length human NRF2 structure were performed to assess the predicted Corilagin-NRF2 interaction. A mouse IIRI model was used to validate selected molecular and histological findings by histology, RT-qPCR, Western blotting, and immunohistochemistry. In IEC-6 cells subjected to OGD/R, NRF2 immunofluorescence and siRNA-mediated knockdown of Nrf2 or Abcg2 were used to further evaluate the involvement of NRF2 and ABCG2 in Corilagin-mediated protection. Intersection analysis identified 472 genes shared among Corilagin-related targets, IIRI-related genes, and ERS-associated genes. Enrichment analysis highlighted stress- and injury-related pathways, including PI3K-Akt signaling. Ensemble machine learning prioritized 12 core genes across human and mouse datasets, with ABCG2, IL10, and PRKCZ emerging as prominent candidates. Docking and 100-ns MD simulations supported persistent Corilagin retention within the predicted NRF2 binding region, while post-relaxation MM/GBSA analysis indicated favorable interaction energetics. In vivo, Corilagin pretreatment reduced inflammation and oxidative stress-related changes, restored apical ABCG2 and tight-junction protein expression, improved mucosal morphology, and altered CHOP expression. In IEC-6 cells, Nrf2 or Abcg2 knockdown weakened Corilagin-mediated preservation of Occludin, Claudin-1, and ZO-1 under OGD/R, supporting NRF2-ABCG2 involvement in this protective response. Corilagin may alleviate IIRI by modulating ERS-related molecular changes and preserving the intestinal epithelial barrier with NRF2 and ABCG2 contributing to a candidate regulatory module involved in this protective response. These findings provide computational and experimental support for further investigation of Corilagin as a potential intervention for IIRI and illustrate the value of combining multi-source data integration with ensemble machine learning to characterize the multitarget pharmacology of natural products.

title: Geometric vs. global knowledge in GNNs: a controlled leakage study for early-late TS classification of the isomerization of the 2-norbornyl carbocation
abstract: Transition-state classification remains challenging because distinguishing reactant-like from product-like geometries requires resolving subtle mechanistic changes. Although GNNs can learn molecular representations, it remains unclear whether their predictions arise from genuine mechanistic information in geometry or from global descriptors that inadvertently encode reaction-coordinate information. A controlled leakage study was performed on the highly interconnected 2-norbornyl carbocation isomerization network, which contains overlapping pathways and complex rearrangement features. A hierarchical series of GNNs was constructed to progressively introduce increasingly informative global descriptors. These descriptors ranged from displacement and force-based metrics to structural-distance relationships and normalized reaction-coordinate fractions. The geometry-only GNN performed near randomly, indicating that local graph representations alone are insufficient for robust early-late TS classification. Adding displacement-based descriptors substantially improved performance, while force-based and redundant descriptors provided only modest additional gains. A sharp increase to near-perfect accuracy occurred after introducing reactant-TS and product-TS structural-distance descriptors, even before explicitly including the normalized reaction fraction. Multiple analyses showed that these chemically meaningful global descriptors can unintentionally encode target-defining reaction-progress information, highlighting the need for systematic leakage detection in graph-based chemical machine learning. The inclusion of electronic properties, such as Mayer bond orders and Mulliken charges increased model accuracy without data leakage. More broadly, this work establishes a systematic framework for identifying and quantifying information leakage in graph-based chemical machine learning.

title: A High-Content Pseudotime Framework for Morphological Profiling of Dengue Virus Inhibitors from a Drug-Repurposing Library
abstract: Dengue virus (DENV) causes dengue fever, a globally prevalent, epidemic-prone disease with no FDA-approved antivirals. Additionally, the available vaccine for DENV can increase the risk of severe dengue fever for those who have never had a DENV infection due to antibody-dependent enhancement. Thus, there is an urgent need to identify DENV antivirals. Drug repurposing, high-content screening, and machine learning were leveraged to efficiently identify antivirals likely to inhibit DENV replication.

title: Quantification of cellular contributions to multi-cellular pattern formation
abstract: Multi-cellular pattern formation is a key process in organism development, regeneration, and disease. Such multi-cellular patterns include, for instance, cell density and gene expression patterns. Here, we develop a cell-track-based method that quantifies how much individual cellular processes contribute to the emergence of large-scale patterns. These cellular processes include changes in cellular expression levels, cell motion, cell divisions, and apoptosis. We validate our method using synthetic data, before demonstrating it on two sets of experimental data. Our method is purely geometric and does not require any mechanistic assumptions about the underlying pattern-forming processes, making it very generic and robust. It thus enables unbiased, data-driven study of the mechanisms driving pattern formation across a broad class of systems.

title: NNGeoGVS: A Unified Equivariant Graph Neural Network Framework for Integrated Structure and Ligand-based Virtual Screening
abstract: IntroductionVirtual screening (VS) is a widely used computational strategy in early- stage drug discovery for identifying bioactive compounds from large chemical libraries. Although structure-based and ligand-based approaches have demonstrated success individually, their integration into a unified deep learning framework remains limited. This study presents NNGeoGVS (Neural Network Geometric Graph-based Virtual Screening), an Equivariant Graph Neural Network (EGNN)-based framework that integrates ligand molecular topology and protein active-site geometry for activity…

title: Crowding governs resistance confinement and guides the improvement of adaptive therapy in a 2D melanoma model system
abstract: The emergence of treatment resistant mutants is one of the primary contributors to therapy failure in cancer. Evolution-based adaptive therapies aim to exploit the competition between sensitive and resistant cells to prolong therapeutic control. However, in the densely packed tissues of solid tumors, competition is not only determined by cell-intrinsic factors but also a result of local physical interactions between neighboring cells. The successful development of physics-informed adaptive therapies therefore hinges upon the bottom-up integration of tissue mechanics and experimentally grounded models of tumor evolution. Here, we show how population-level treatment response emerges from mechanical interactions between individual cells.
